passages.name: 2021年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 在玩耍中培养21世纪技能
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与科技
passages.summary: 教育工作者希望让学生为成功的未来做好准备，科技公司有意培养具备STEM技能的劳动力队伍，而玩耍或许能让双方携手实现这些目标。文章指出，STEM技能与传统的、亲自动手的创造性活动结合起来时，会得到增强，也更有实际意义；许多专家认为，21世纪最重要的技能与创造力有关，而这些技能是孩子在鼓捣小玩意时习得的。搭积木这类玩耍有助于孩子发现并逐步掌握数学和几何中的关键原理。如果玩耍和搭建对21世纪技能的发展至关重要，那么培养这些技能或许只需给孩子留出玩耍和鼓捣的空间，并不需要21世纪的技术，这一点对资源不足的学校和社区尤为重要。

paras.en: Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem.
paras.zh: 教育工作者和企业领导者的共同点，比人们可能以为的要多。

w.m: 比人们可能以为的（更……）；比看上去（更……）

paras.en: Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future.
paras.zh: 教师希望让学生为成功的未来做好准备。

paras.en: Technology companies have an interest in developing a workforce with the STEM (science, technology, engineering and math) skills needed to grow the company and advance the industry.
paras.zh: 科技公司有意培养一支劳动力队伍，使其具备发展壮大公司、推动行业进步所需的STEM（科学、技术、工程和数学）技能。

w.m: n. 科学、技术、工程和数学（的统称）

paras.en: How can they work together to achieve these goals?
paras.zh: 双方如何才能携手实现这些目标呢？

paras.en: Play may be the answer.
paras.zh: 玩耍或许就是答案。

paras.en: Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities.
paras.zh: 注重STEM技能固然重要，但现实情况是，STEM技能与传统的、亲自动手的创造性活动结合起来时，会得到增强，也更有实际意义。

w.m: adj. 有实际意义的；相关的
adj. 亲自动手的；实践的

paras.en: This combination is proving to be the best way to prepare today’s children to be the makers and builders of tomorrow.
paras.zh: 事实日益证明，要让如今的孩子做好准备，成为未来的创客和建造者，这种结合是最好的办法。

paras.en: That is why technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good old-fashioned play.
paras.zh: 正因如此，科技公司正与教育工作者合作，找回美好的老式玩耍。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此

paras.en: In fact many experts argue that the most important 21st-century skills aren’t related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity: skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem-solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and take risks.
paras.zh: 事实上，许多专家认为，21世纪最重要的技能与具体的技术或学科内容无关，而与创造力有关：想象力、发现问题和解决问题的能力、团队合作、乐观、耐心，以及尝试和冒险的能力等技能。

paras.en: These are skills acquired when kids tinker (鼓捣小玩意).
paras.zh: 这些是孩子们在鼓捣小玩意时习得的技能。

paras.en: High-tech organizations such as NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory have found that their best overall problem solvers were master tinkerers in their youth.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局喷气推进实验室等高科技机构发现，机构中解决问题综合能力最强的人，年轻时曾是鼓捣小玩意的高手。

w.m: n. 美国国家航空航天局
adj. 技艺高超的；精通的
n. 爱鼓捣小玩意的人

paras.en: There are cognitive (认知的) benefits of doing things the way we did as children—building something, tearing it down, then building it up again.
paras.zh: 像我们小时候那样做事，对认知有好处：搭建一样东西，把它拆掉，然后再重新搭起来。

paras.en: Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities.
paras.zh: 研究表明，如果给四五岁的孩子15分钟的自由玩耍时间，他们会用其中三分之一的时间从事空间、数学和建筑类活动。

w.m: v. 给予（given 为过去分词，表条件：如果给……）

paras.en: This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry.
paras.zh: 这类玩耍，尤其是搭积木，有助于孩子发现并逐步掌握数学和几何中的关键原理。

paras.en: If play and building are critical to 21st-century skill development, that’s really good news for two reasons: Children are born builders, makers, and creators, so fostering (培养) 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out, even as they grow older.
paras.zh: 如果玩耍和搭建对21世纪技能的发展至关重要，那么这真是个好消息，原因有二：孩子天生就是建造者、创客和创造者，因此，培养21世纪技能或许简单到只需给孩子留出空间，让他们去玩耍、鼓捣、尝试各种东西，即使在他们渐渐长大的时候也一样。

w.m: 即使在……的时候；就在……的同时

paras.en: Secondly, it doesn’t take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills.
paras.zh: 其次，培养21世纪技能并不需要21世纪的技术。

w.m: 做某事需要……（此处为否定）

paras.en: This is especially important for under-resourced schools and communities.
paras.zh: 这对资源不足的学校和社区来说尤为重要。

paras.en: Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important “maker” skills.
paras.zh: 拿起手边现成的任何材料鼓捣一番，是调动那些重要“创客”技能的一种简单方法。

paras.en: And anyone, anywhere, can do it.
paras.zh: 而且无论是谁、无论在哪里，都能做到。

passages.name: 2021年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 不可忽视员工的IT使用体验
passages.genre: 议论文 · 职场与科技
passages.summary: 作者并不羡慕IT工作者：他们得在关键会议中途立刻修好投影仪，得忍受同事的坏脾气，还明知有更好的系统，雇主却不肯拿出资金购买。调查显示，工作依赖IT支持的员工把IT视为对工作不满的一大根源；IT正常运转时员工的自信心会高涨，工作满意度也可能飙升，而出了差错的IT改造项目会引发员工普遍的挫败感。作者认为，管理者应重视IT用户体验对员工的影响，并提供充分、及时的IT支持，IT从业者也需要了解员工使用IT时的心理感受；企业应让IT基础设施适应员工的工作，而不是调整员工的工作去适应公司IT的局限。

paras.en: Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy.
paras.zh: 做信息技术（即IT）工作者，这份工作我并不羡慕。

paras.en: IT workers are the ones who, right in the middle of a critical meeting, are expected to instantly fix the projector that’s no longer working.
paras.zh: 关键会议正开到一半，投影仪却不工作了，这时被指望立刻把它修好的，就是IT工作者。

w.m: adj. 关键的；至关重要的

paras.en: They have to tolerate the bad tempers of colleagues frustrated at the number of times they’ve had to call the help desk for the same issue.
paras.zh: 他们不得不忍受同事的坏脾气：为了同一个问题，同事们已经不得不一次又一次地打电话找服务台，为此恼火不已。

paras.en: They are also the ones who know there are systems that are more powerful, more reliable and faster, but their employer simply will not put up the funds to buy them.
paras.zh: 也正是他们知道，有些系统更强大、更可靠、速度更快，可雇主就是不肯拿出资金来购买。

w.m: adv. 简直；就是（加强否定语气）

paras.en: According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction.
paras.zh: 根据最近的一项调查，工作依赖IT支持的员工认为，IT是他们对工作不满的一大根源。

paras.en: Through no fault of their own, they can suddenly find their productivity deteriorating or quality control non-existent.
paras.zh: 这并不是他们自己的过错，他们却可能突然发现自己的工作效率不断下滑，或者质量控制荡然无存。

w.h: through no fault of one's own

paras.en: And there’s little they can do about it.
paras.zh: 而对此，他们几乎无能为力。

w.h: there's little one can do about

paras.en: The experience of using IT penetrates almost the entire work field.
paras.zh: 使用IT的体验几乎渗透到了整个工作领域。

paras.en: It has become a crucial part of employees’ overall work experience.
paras.zh: 它已经成为员工整体工作体验中至关重要的一部分。

paras.en: When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells.
paras.zh: IT正常运转的时候，员工的自信心就会高涨。

paras.en: Their job satisfaction, too, can surge when well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes.
paras.zh: 运转良好的机器让员工摆脱枯燥的任务或重复的流程时，他们的工作满意度也可能飙升。

paras.en: But if there’s one thing that triggers widespread employee frustration, it’s an IT transformation project gone wrong, where swollen expectations have been popped and a long list of promised efficiencies has been reversed.
paras.zh: 但如果说有哪件事会引发员工普遍的挫败感，那就是出了差错的IT改造项目：膨胀的期望被戳破，原先承诺的一长串效率提升也不进反退。

w.m: n. 效率；（复数）效率提升

paras.en: This occurs when business leaders implement IT initiatives with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user.
paras.zh: 企业领导者在推行IT新举措时，如果几乎不考虑这些变化会给终端用户带来什么影响，就会出现这种情况。

paras.en: Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes.
paras.zh: 正因如此，管理者应该充分认识到IT用户体验对员工的影响究竟有多大，并投入大量精力，确保自己的IT团队消除编程错误和应用程序崩溃。

w.m: 这就是为什么；正因如此
adj. 有影响力的；影响大的

paras.en: Adequate and timely IT support should also be available to enable users to cope with technological issues at work.
paras.zh: 还应该提供充分、及时的IT支持，使用户能够应对工作中的技术问题。

paras.en: More importantly, IT practitioners need to understand what employees experience mentally when they use IT.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，IT从业者需要了解员工在使用IT时有怎样的心理感受。

paras.en: Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees’ work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company’s IT limitations.
paras.zh: 因此，企业需要搭建好自己的IT基础设施，使其在设计上适应员工的工作，而不是调整员工的工作去适应公司IT的局限。

passages.name: 2021年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 营养研究背后的行业资助
passages.genre: 议论文 · 饮食与健康
passages.summary: 本周有内幕曝光：50年前，制糖业曾出钱请哈佛大学科学家做研究，这些研究把焦点从糖在心脏病中的作用上移开，转向了膳食脂肪，许多美国人为此震惊。而可能让消费者意外的是，如今仍有大量营养学研究由食品行业资助：内斯特尔非正式追踪的近170项此类研究中，约90%偏向资助方的利益。文章还列举了韦尔奇食品公司、桂格燕麦公司和可口可乐公司的资助事例。作者认为，消费者应对最新的营养研究发现持怀疑态度；利布曼建议信赖审视过全部证据的健康专家，并以政府官方的《膳食指南》为例，该指南以对数百项研究的综述为依据；内斯特尔则表示，专家的建议依然相当简单。

paras.en: Sugar shocked.
paras.zh: 被糖震惊了。

paras.en: That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar’s role in heart disease—and put the spotlight (注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat.
paras.zh: 这正是本周许多美国人在相关内幕曝光后的反应：50年前，制糖业曾出钱请哈佛大学的科学家做研究，这些研究把焦点从糖在心脏病中的作用上移开，并将关注的中心直接对准了膳食脂肪。

paras.en: What might surprise consumers is just how many present-day nutrition studies are still funded by the food industry.
paras.zh: 可能让消费者感到意外的是，时至今日，竟然仍有如此多的营养学研究由食品行业资助。

w.m: v. 使感到意外；使吃惊

paras.en: Nutrition scholar Marion Nestle of New York University spent a year informally tracking industry-funded studies on food.
paras.zh: 纽约大学营养学学者玛丽恩·内斯特尔花了一年时间，以非正式的方式追踪由行业资助的食品研究。

paras.en: “Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor’s interest,” Nestle tells us.
paras.zh: “在近170项研究中，约90%偏向资助方的利益，”内斯特尔告诉我们。

paras.en: Other systematic reviews support her conclusions.
paras.zh: 其他系统性综述也支持她的结论。

paras.en: For instance, studies funded by Welch Foods—the brand behind Welch’s 100% Grape Juice—found that drinking Concord grape juice daily may boost brain function.
paras.zh: 例如，韦尔奇食品公司（即韦尔奇100%葡萄汁背后的品牌）资助的研究发现，每天喝康科德葡萄汁可能会增强大脑功能。

paras.en: Another, funded by Quaker Oats, concluded, as a Daily Mail story put it, that “hot oatmeal (燕麦粥) breakfast keeps you full for longer.”
paras.zh: 另一项研究由桂格燕麦公司资助，用《每日邮报》一篇报道的话来说，其结论是“早餐吃热燕麦粥能让你饱得更久”。

paras.en: Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca-Cola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink.
paras.zh: 去年，《纽约时报》披露了可口可乐公司如何资助知名科学家和机构，而这些科学家和机构所宣扬的观点是：在对抗体重增加的斗争中，人们应该多关注运动，少关注自己吃什么、喝什么。

w.m: n. 观点；（要传达的）信息

paras.en: Coca-Cola also released data detailing its funding of several medical institutions and associations between 2010 and 2015.
paras.zh: 可口可乐公司还公布了数据，详细列出了它在2010年至2015年间对几家医疗机构和协会的资助。

paras.en: “It’s certainly a problem that so much research in nutrition and health is funded by industry,” says Bonnie Liebman, director of nutrition at the Center for Science in the Public Interest.
paras.zh: “营养与健康领域有这么多研究由产业界资助，这无疑是个问题，”公共利益科学中心营养部主任邦妮·利布曼说。

paras.en: “When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for.”
paras.zh: “食品行业出钱资助研究时，往往是花钱买什么，就得到什么。”

w.m: 花钱买什么就得到什么；一分钱一分货

paras.en: And what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding.
paras.zh: 而它花钱买的，往往是对该行业有利的研究发现。

w.m: adj. 对（该）行业有利的；偏向行业的
n. 研究发现；研究结果

paras.en: Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical (怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on their news feed.
paras.zh: 鉴于这样的环境，消费者在读到营养科学的最新发现时应该持怀疑态度，并对新闻推送里冒出来的最新研究置之不理。

paras.en: “Rely on health experts who’ve reviewed all the evidence,” Liebman says, pointing to the official government Dietary Guidelines, which are based on reviews of hundreds of studies.
paras.zh: “要信赖那些审视过全部证据的健康专家，”利布曼说，并举出政府官方的《膳食指南》为例，该指南以对数百项研究的综述为依据。

paras.en: “And that expert advice remains pretty simple,” says Nestle.
paras.zh: “而专家给出的这些建议依然相当简单，”内斯特尔说。

paras.en: “We know what healthy diets are—lots of vegetables, not too much junk food, balanced calories.
paras.zh: “我们知道健康的饮食是什么样的——多吃蔬菜，别吃太多垃圾食品，热量均衡。

paras.en: Everything else is really difficult to do experimentally.”
paras.zh: 除此之外的一切，都真的很难通过实验来研究。”

w.m: adv. 通过实验；用实验方法

passages.name: 2021年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 成功的新定义与零工经济
passages.genre: 议论文 · 职场与经济
passages.summary: 过去，成功被定义为在一家公司长期任职、沿着公司的职位阶梯步步晋升，目标是登上顶层、积累财富，然后退休，过上安逸的生活；作者刚参加工作时，不每隔三四年换一次公司就根本无法在事业上取得进展，但做顾问或自由职业者仍会让人纳闷这个人出了什么问题。如今，同时为五家企业做顾问或从事自由职业是一种荣誉的象征，许多公司指望这类专业人士解决全职团队解决不了的问题，或只为特定项目聘用他们以节省开支；人们也日益认识到，兼顾工作与娱乐、从事自己所热爱之事的人更专注、更高效。作者认为，现在需要一个专为撮合自由职业者与客户而设计的交易平台，这类平台缓慢而稳步地在传统企业与新兴的零工经济之间架起桥梁。或许更重要的是，随着全球经济不断受到技术和其他巨大变化的冲击，零工经济本身将成为经济与社会变革的引擎。

paras.en: Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder.
paras.zh: 成功一度被定义为能在一家公司长期任职，并沿着公司的职位阶梯步步晋升。

paras.en: The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease.
paras.zh: 当时的目标是登上顶层、积累财富，然后退休，过上安逸的生活。

w.m: 登上顶层；达到最高位置

paras.en: My father is a successful senior executive.
paras.zh: 我父亲是一位事业有成的高级主管。

w.m: adj. 成功的；事业有成的
n. 主管；高级管理人员

paras.en: In 35 years, he worked for only three companies.
paras.zh: 35年里，他只为三家公司工作过。

paras.en: When I started my career, things were already different.
paras.zh: 我开始职业生涯时，情况就已经不同了。

paras.en: If you weren’t changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren’t getting ahead in your career.
paras.zh: 如果你不每隔三四年换一次公司，就根本无法在事业上取得进展。

w.m: 无法取得进展；不能出人头地

paras.en: But back then, if you were a consultant or freelancer (自由职业者), people would wonder what was wrong with you.
paras.zh: 但在当时，如果你是顾问或自由职业者，人们就会纳闷你出了什么问题。

paras.en: They would assume you had problems getting a job.
paras.zh: 他们会以为你找工作有困难。

paras.en: Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor.
paras.zh: 如今，同时为五家企业做顾问或从事自由职业，是一种荣誉的象征。

paras.en: It shows how valuable an individual is.
paras.zh: 这表明了一个人的价值有多大。

paras.en: Many companies now look to these “ultimate professionals” to solve problems their full-time teams can’t.
paras.zh: 现在，许多公司指望这些“顶级专业人士”来解决自家全职团队解决不了的问题。

w.m: 指望……做某事；依靠……来做某事
adj. 顶级的；最好的；终极的

paras.en: Or they save money by hiring “top-tier (顶尖的) experts” only for particular projects.
paras.zh: 或者，它们只为特定项目聘用“顶尖专家”，以此节省开支。

paras.en: Working at home or in cafes, starting businesses of their own, and even launching business ventures that eventually may fail all indicate “initiative,” “creativity,” and “adaptability,” which are desirable qualities in today’s workplace.
paras.zh: 在家或在咖啡馆工作、自己创办企业，甚至开创最终可能失败的商业项目，都显示出“主动性”“创造力”和“适应能力”，而这些都是当今职场上受青睐的品质。

w.m: adj. 受青睐的；值得拥有的；可取的

paras.en: Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，人们日益认识到，那些兼顾工作与娱乐、从事自己所热爱之事的人更专注、更高效，从而为客户带来更大的价值。

w.m: adj. 日益增长的；越来越多的
adj. 专注的；目标明确的
adj. 高效的；富有成效的

paras.en: Who are these people?
paras.zh: 这些都是些什么人呢？

paras.en: They are artists, writers, programmers, providers of office services and career advice.
paras.zh: 他们是艺术家、作家、程序员，以及提供办公服务和职业建议的人。

paras.en: What’s needed now is a marketplace platform specifically designed to bring freelancers and clients together.
paras.zh: 现在需要的是一个专为撮合自由职业者与客户而设计的交易平台。

paras.en: Such platforms then become a place to feature the most experienced, professional, and creative talent.
paras.zh: 这样一来，此类平台就成为展示最有经验、最专业、最具创造力的人才的场所。

w.m: adj. 有经验的；经验丰富的

paras.en: This is where they conduct business, where a sense of community reinforces the culture and values of the gig economy (零工经济), and where success is rewarded with good reviews that encourage more business.
paras.zh: 他们在这里开展业务；在这里，社群意识强化着零工经济的文化和价值观；也是在这里，成功会以好评的形式得到回报，这些好评又会促成更多生意。

w.m: 这里就是……的地方；在这里……
以……作为回报；得到……的回报

paras.en: Slowly but surely, these platforms create a bridge between traditional enterprises and this emerging economy.
paras.zh: 这些平台缓慢而稳步地在传统企业与这一新兴经济之间架起桥梁。

paras.en: Perhaps more important, as the global economy continues to be disrupted by technology and other massive change, the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation.
paras.zh: 或许更重要的是，随着全球经济不断受到技术和其他巨大变化的冲击，零工经济本身将成为经济与社会变革的引擎。

passages.name: 2021年6月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 无聊背后可能藏着未满足的需求
passages.genre: 议论文 · 心理与生活
passages.summary: 研究指出，无聊有益于创造力、创新和心理健康，但作者认为，这些好处实际上可能与有时间放空头脑、安静下来或做白日梦有关。作者指出，无聊可能表明你有某种需求没有得到满足，比如对归属感和意义感的需求。作者建议加入组织，建立面对面的人际关系；寻找能做出独特贡献的工作，或用自己的时间和才能去支持某项事业。如果你对无聊的定义是安静、专注当下和沉思内省，那就继续保持；但如果你正苦于真正的无聊，不妨考虑寻求新的人际联系和更有意义的挑战，正是这些事情会真正缓解无聊。

paras.en: Boredom has become trendy.
paras.zh: 无聊已经变得时髦起来。

paras.en: Studies point to how boredom is good for creativity and innovation, as well as mental health.
paras.zh: 多项研究指出，无聊有益于创造力和创新，对心理健康也有好处。

paras.en: It is found that people are more creative following the completion of a tedious task.
paras.zh: 据发现，人们在完成一项乏味的任务之后会更有创造力。

paras.en: When people are bored, they have an increase in “associative thought”—the process of making new connections between ideas, which is linked to innovative thinking.
paras.zh: 人们感到无聊时，“联想思维”会增多——联想思维是在不同想法之间建立新联系的过程，与创新思维有关。

w.m: adj. 感到无聊的；厌倦的

paras.en: These studies are impressive, but in reality, the benefits of boredom may be related to having time to clear your mind, be quiet, or daydream.
paras.zh: 这些研究令人印象深刻，但实际上，无聊的好处可能与有时间放空头脑、安静下来或做白日梦有关。

paras.en: In our stimulation-rich world, it seems unrealistic that boredom could occur at all.
paras.zh: 在我们这个充满刺激的世界里，无聊竟然还会出现，这似乎不现实。

paras.en: Yet, there are valid reasons boredom may feel so painful.
paras.zh: 然而，无聊之所以可能让人感觉如此痛苦，是有其合理原因的。

paras.en: As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn’t being met.
paras.zh: 事实证明，无聊可能表明这样一个事实：你有某种需求没有得到满足。

paras.en: Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging.
paras.zh: 我们这个时刻在线的社交媒体世界或许会带来更多的人际联系，但这些联系很肤浅，还可能妨碍我们建立真正的归属感。

paras.en: Feeling bored may signal the desire for a greater sense of community and the feeling that you fit in with others around you.
paras.zh: 感到无聊可能表明，你渴望获得更强的集体感，渴望感到自己能融入身边的人群。

paras.en: So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships.
paras.zh: 那就迈出一步，加入一个组织，去建立面对面的人际关系吧。

w.m: 迈出……的一步；采取……的行动

paras.en: You’ll find depth that you won’t get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post.
paras.zh: 你会体会到一种深度，无论你的帖子收获多少点赞，这种深度都是屏幕给不了你的。

paras.en: As with the need for belonging, bored people often report that they feel a limited sense of meaning.
paras.zh: 和对归属感的需求一样，感到无聊的人常常表示，他们觉得意义感有限。

paras.en: It’s a fundamental human need to have a larger purpose and to feel like we’re part of something bigger than ourselves.
paras.zh: 拥有更远大的目标，感觉自己是某种比自身更宏大的事物的一部分，这是人类的一种基本需求。

paras.en: When people are bored, they’re more likely to feel less meaning in their lives.
paras.zh: 人们感到无聊时，更有可能觉得自己的生活没那么有意义。

paras.en: If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent.
paras.zh: 如果你想减少无聊、增强意义感，就去寻找一份能让你做出独特贡献的工作，或者找到一项你可以用自己的时间和才能去支持的事业。

paras.en: If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective, keep it up.
paras.zh: 如果你对无聊的定义是安静、专注当下、沉思内省，那就继续保持吧。

w.m: adj. 专注当下的；有正念的

paras.en: But if you’re struggling with real boredom and the emptiness it provokes, consider whether you might seek new connections and more significant challenges.
paras.zh: 但如果你正苦于真正的无聊以及它引发的空虚感，那就考虑一下，你是否可以去寻求新的人际联系和更有意义的挑战。

paras.en: These are the things that will genuinely relieve boredom and make you more effective in the process.
paras.zh: 正是这些事情会真正缓解无聊，并在此过程中让你做事更有成效。

passages.name: 2021年6月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 人们为何少报自己吃的东西
passages.genre: 说明文 · 饮食与健康
passages.summary: 作者早在2016年就怀疑人们会漏掉自己吃过的东西，并找到可靠证据，表明人们大幅少报了自己吃的东西；如今国家统计局证实，我们摄入的热量比国家统计数据所称的多50%。作者指出了至少三个可能的原因：肥胖水平上升、试图减肥的人所占比例增加，以及吃零食和在外就餐增多。作者建议，在统计上投资于更准确的测量方案，在政策上把重点放在能让人们轻松少摄入热量的方案上，并寻找新办法，确保人们吃的东西不会对腰围产生太大影响。

paras.en: Can you remember what you ate yesterday?
paras.zh: 你还记得自己昨天吃了什么吗？

paras.en: If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner.
paras.zh: 要是有人问起，大多数人都能含糊地描述一下自己的几顿正餐：早餐、午餐、晚餐。

paras.en: But can you be sure you’ve noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk?
paras.zh: 但你能确定自己记下了在车里吃的每一根零食棒，或是在办公桌前吃的每一把坚果吗？

paras.en: Most people will have a feeling that they’ve missed something out.
paras.zh: 大多数人都会感觉自己漏掉了些什么。

paras.en: We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades.
paras.zh: 我们最初产生这种怀疑，还是早在2016年，当时国家统计数据显示，过去几十年间热量摄入量大幅下降，这一事实令我们困惑不解。

w.m: n. 卡路里；（食物的）热量

paras.en: We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate.
paras.zh: 我们找到了可靠的证据，表明人们一直在大幅少报自己吃的东西。

paras.en: Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.
paras.zh: 如今，国家统计局已经证实，我们摄入的热量比我们的国家统计数据所称的多50%。

paras.en: Why is this happening?
paras.zh: 为什么会出现这种情况？

paras.en: We can point to at least three potential causes.
paras.zh: 我们可以指出至少三个可能的原因。

paras.en: One is the rise in obesity levels itself.
paras.zh: 其一是肥胖水平本身的上升。

paras.en: Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.
paras.zh: 肥胖者的少报率要高得多，原因很简单：他们吃的食物更多，因而要记住的也更多。

w.m: adv. 只是；仅仅（表示原因很简单）

paras.en: Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time.
paras.zh: 另一个原因是，试图减肥的人所占的比例随着时间的推移一直在上升。

paras.en: People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not.
paras.zh: 想减肥的人更有可能少报自己吃的东西，无论他们是否超重。

paras.en: This may be driven partly by self-deception or “wishful thinking”.
paras.zh: 这可能在一定程度上源于自我欺骗或“一厢情愿的想法”。

w.m: adv. 部分地；在一定程度上
一厢情愿的想法；痴心妄想

paras.en: The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake.
paras.zh: 最后一个可能的原因是，近几十年来，吃零食和在外就餐的情况增多了——既体现在频率上，也体现在它们占我们总能量摄入的比重上。

paras.en: Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.
paras.zh: 同样，有证据表明，在外面吃的食物是调查中记录质量最差的类别之一。

paras.en: So, what’s the message conveyed?
paras.zh: 那么，这传达出什么信息呢？

paras.en: For statistics, we should invest in more accurate measurement options.
paras.zh: 在统计方面，我们应该投资于更准确的测量方案。

w.m: n. 统计（工作）；统计数据
n. 方案；可选择的事物

paras.en: For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories.
paras.zh: 在政策方面，我们需要把重点放在那些能让人们轻松少摄入热量的方案上。

paras.en: If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet.
paras.zh: 如果人们不清楚自己吃了多少，就可能真的很难坚持节食。

w.m: n. 节食；（为减肥等而规定的）饮食

paras.en: Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat won’t have much impact on their waistlines.
paras.zh: 此外，我们应该寻找新办法，确保人们吃的东西不会对腰围产生太大影响。

paras.en: If this works, it won’t matter if they can’t remember what they ate yesterday.
paras.zh: 如果这能奏效，那么即便人们记不起自己昨天吃了什么，也无关紧要了。

passages.name: 2021年12月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 远程办公的成本由谁承担
passages.genre: 议论文 · 经济与社会
passages.summary: 雇主称员工转为居家办公能为其大幅节省房地产开支，但作者认为，这些节省的开支源于把成本转嫁给员工；如果员工得不到充分补偿，这可能变成寄生资本主义的一种变体。作者以蒙特利尔为例做了粗略估算，发现雇主节省的开支与员工在家设立办公室应得的补偿价值相近。员工一旦得到合理补偿，雇主节省的开支就会很有限，在办公室工作的诸多优势将促使雇主搁置远程办公的想法。

paras.en: As many office workers adapt to remote work, cities may undergo fundamental change if offices remain under-utilized.
paras.zh: 随着许多上班族适应远程办公，如果办公室继续得不到充分利用，城市可能会经历根本性的变化。

w.m: v. 仍然是；保持（某种状态）
adj. 未得到充分利用的

paras.en: Who will benefit if working from home becomes the norm?
paras.zh: 如果居家办公成为常态，谁会从中受益？

paras.en: Employers argue they make considerable savings on real estate when workers shift from office to home work.
paras.zh: 雇主们声称，员工从办公室办公转为居家办公时，他们能在房地产上大幅节省开支。

paras.en: However, these savings result from passing costs on to workers.
paras.zh: 然而，这些节省的开支源于把成本转嫁给员工。

paras.en: Unless employees are fully compensated, this could become a variant of parasitic (寄生的) capitalism, whereby corporate profits increasingly rely on extracting value from the public—and now personal—realm, rather than on generating new value.
paras.zh: 除非员工得到充分补偿，否则这可能变成寄生资本主义的一种变体，即企业利润越来越依赖于从公共领域、如今也从个人领域榨取价值，而不是依靠创造新价值。

w.m: adv. 借此；由此（指借助某种方式）

paras.en: Though employers are backed by a chorus of remote work advocates, others note the loneliness, reduced productivity and inefficiencies of extended remote work.
paras.zh: 尽管雇主得到一众远程办公倡导者的齐声支持，另一些人却指出了长期远程办公存在的孤独感、生产率下降和种种低效问题。

w.m: 一片（……之声）；一群齐声附和的……
adj. 降低了的；减少了的
n. 低效；效率低下之处

paras.en: If working from home becomes permanent, employees will have to dedicate part of their private space to work.
paras.zh: 如果居家办公成为一种永久性的安排，员工就不得不把自己的一部分私人空间专门用于工作。

paras.en: This requires purchasing desks, chairs and office equipment.
paras.zh: 这就需要购置书桌、椅子和办公设备。

paras.en: It also means having private space dedicated to work: the space must be heated, cleaned, maintained and paid for.
paras.zh: 这还意味着要有专门用于工作的私人空间：必须给这块空间供暖、打扫和维护，还要为它付钱。

paras.en: The cost depends on many things, but for purposes of illustration, I have run some estimates for Montreal.
paras.zh: 这笔费用取决于很多因素，但为了举例说明，我针对蒙特利尔做了一些估算。

w.m: v. 进行（计算、测试等）；做

paras.en: The exercise is simple but important, since it brings these costs out of the realm of speculation into the realm of meaningful discussion.
paras.zh: 这项测算虽然简单，却很重要，因为它把这些成本从猜测的范畴带进了有意义的讨论范畴。

w.m: n. （为某一目的进行的）活动；工作

paras.en: Rough calculations show that the savings made by employers when their staff works from home are of similar value to the compensation workers should receive for setting up offices at home.
paras.zh: 粗略计算表明，员工居家办公时雇主节省的开支，与员工因在家设立办公室而应得的补偿价值相近。

paras.en: What does this mean for offices in cities?
paras.zh: 这对城市里的办公室意味着什么？

paras.en: One of two things may happen: Employers pass these costs on to employees.
paras.zh: 可能会出现两种情况之一：雇主把这些成本转嫁给员工。

paras.en: This would be a form of expropriation (侵占), with employees absorbing production costs that have traditionally been paid by the employer.
paras.zh: 这将是某种形式的侵占：员工要承担传统上一直由雇主支付的生产成本。

w.m: 某种形式的……；……的一种形式
v. 承担（费用、损失等）；吸收

paras.en: This represents a considerable transfer of value from employees to employers.
paras.zh: 这代表着大量价值从员工手中转移到雇主手中。

paras.en: When employees are properly compensated, employers’ real estate savings will be modest.
paras.zh: 员工一旦得到合理补偿，雇主在房地产上节省的开支就会很有限。

paras.en: If savings are modest, then the many advantages of working in offices—such as a lively atmosphere, rapidity of communication, team-building and acclimatization (适应环境) of new employees—will encourage employers to shelve the idea of remote work and, like Yahoo in 2013, encourage employees to work most of the time from corporate office space.
paras.zh: 如果节省的开支很有限，那么在办公室工作的诸多优势——比如活跃的氛围、快速的沟通、团队建设以及新员工对环境的适应——就会促使雇主搁置远程办公的想法，并像雅虎在2013年那样，鼓励员工大部分时间在公司的办公场所工作。

w.m: adj. 活跃的；充满生气的

passages.name: 2021年12月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 好奇心：发展动力与潜在代价
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与成长
passages.summary: 人类对知识的渴求推动了我们这个物种的成功发展，但好奇心也可能带来危险。科学家很难给好奇心下定义，但普遍的共识是，它是某种收集信息的手段，心理学家也一致认为它由内在动机驱动；好奇心还含有遗传成分。婴儿偏爱新奇事物，好奇心是帮助他们在短时间内学习大量信息的工具之一。不过，好奇心往往伴随着代价：有时代价很小，比如婴儿学走路时经常摔倒；有时尝试新想法却可能导致灾难。

paras.en: The human thirst for knowledge is the driving force behind our successful development as a species.
paras.zh: 人类对知识的渴求，是我们作为一个物种得以成功发展的驱动力。

paras.en: But curiosity can also be dangerous, leading to setbacks or even downfalls.
paras.zh: 但好奇心也可能很危险，会导致挫折，甚至招致毁灭。

paras.en: Given curiosity’s complexity, scientists have found it hard to define.
paras.zh: 鉴于好奇心的复杂性，科学家们一直觉得很难给它下定义。

paras.en: While pinning down a definition has proven tricky, the general consensus is it’s some means of information gathering.
paras.zh: 虽然事实证明，确定好奇心的定义颇为棘手，但普遍的共识是，它是某种收集信息的手段。

paras.en: Psychologists also agree curiosity is intrinsically (内在地) motivated.
paras.zh: 心理学家们还一致认为，好奇心是由内在动机驱动的。

w.m: adj. 有动机的；受（某种动机）驱动的

paras.en: Curiosity covers such a large set of behaviors that there probably isn’t any single “curiosity gene” that makes humans wonder about and explore their environment.
paras.zh: 好奇心涵盖的行为如此广泛，以至于很可能并不存在任何单一的“好奇心基因”，能让人类对周围环境感到好奇并加以探索。

paras.en: That said, curiosity does have a genetic component.
paras.zh: 话虽如此，好奇心确实含有遗传成分。

paras.en: Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways to shape individuals and guide their behavior, including their curiosity.
paras.zh: 基因与环境以许多复杂的方式相互作用，塑造个体并引导其行为，其中也包括好奇心。

paras.en: Regardless of their genetic makeup, infants have to learn an incredible amount of information in a short time, and curiosity is one of the tools humans have found to accomplish that gigantic task.
paras.zh: 无论基因构成如何，婴儿都必须在短时间内学习数量惊人的信息，好奇心则是人类为完成这项庞大任务而找到的工具之一。

w.m: adj. 惊人的；难以置信的

paras.en: Hundreds of studies show that infants prefer novelty.
paras.zh: 数百项研究表明，婴儿偏爱新奇事物。

paras.en: It’s what motivates non-human animals, human infants and probably human adults to explore and seek out new things before growing less interested in them after continued exposure.
paras.zh: 正是这种对新奇事物的偏好，驱使非人类动物、人类婴儿，很可能还有人类成年人，去探索、寻找新事物，而在持续接触之后，他们对这些事物的兴趣又会逐渐减弱。

paras.en: But curiosity often comes with a cost.
paras.zh: 但好奇心往往伴随着代价。

paras.en: In some situations, the stakes are low and failure is a healthy part of growth.
paras.zh: 在有些情况下，利害关系不大，失败是成长中有益的一部分。

paras.en: For instance, many babies are perfectly proficient crawlers, but they decide to try walking because there’s more to see and do when they stand upright.
paras.zh: 例如，许多婴儿爬得非常熟练，却决定尝试走路，因为站直身子时，能看、能做的东西更多。

w.m: n. 爬行者（此处指会爬的婴儿）

paras.en: But this milestone comes at a small cost.
paras.zh: 但达到这一里程碑，是要付出一点小代价的。

paras.en: A study of 12- to 19-month-olds learning how to walk documented that these children fell down a lot.
paras.zh: 一项研究以12到19个月大、正在学走路的幼儿为对象，记录到这些孩子经常摔倒。

w.m: v. （以文字等形式）记录；记载

paras.en: Seventeen times per hour, to be exact.
paras.zh: 确切地说，是每小时十七次。

paras.en: But walking is faster than crawling, so this motivates expert crawlers to transition to walking.
paras.zh: 但走路比爬行快，所以这会促使爬行高手过渡到走路。

w.m: n. 爬行者（此处指会爬的婴儿）

paras.en: Sometimes, however, testing out a new idea can lead to disaster.
paras.zh: 然而，有时候，尝试一个新想法可能会导致灾难。

paras.en: For instance, the Inuit people of the Arctic regions have created incredible ways to deal with the challenges of living in northern climates, but what we forget about are the tens of thousands of people that tried and failed to make it in those challenging landscapes.
paras.zh: 例如，北极地区的因纽特人创造了令人惊叹的方法，来应对在北方气候中生活的种种挑战；但我们忘记的是，还有数以万计的人曾试图在那些充满挑战的地域立足，却以失败告终。

w.m: adj. 充满挑战的；艰巨的

passages.name: 2022年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 网络课程未能提供真正的教育
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与学习
passages.summary: 作者在去年秋季学期选修了一门网络课程，之后逐渐意识到网络课程只不过是满足课程要求的一种手段。文章指出，学生缺乏学习的愿望；大部分作业简短容易，目的是便于评分；师生之间缺少面对面的互动，学生之间的互动也很少；而且并非所有学生都能用上所需的电脑和网络。作者承认网络课程能帮助原本无法到教室上课的学生，但认为它注重便利而非批判性思维，未能提供真正的教育，主张重新构建网络课程。

paras.en: Online classes began to be popularized just a few decades ago.
paras.zh: 仅仅几十年前，网络课程才开始普及。

paras.en: They are advertised as a way for adults to finish their education and students to learn the material at their own pace—it is far more compatible with people’s busy schedules.
paras.zh: 网络课程被宣传为一种途径，让成年人能够完成学业，让学生能够按自己的节奏学习课程内容——这种方式与人们繁忙的日程安排要契合得多。

paras.en: But after being enrolled in an online course last fall semester, I came to realize online classes were merely a means to fulfil course requirements.
paras.zh: 但去年秋季学期选修了一门网络课程之后，我逐渐意识到，网络课程只不过是满足课程要求的一种手段。

w.m: v. 满足（要求、条件）；履行

paras.en: First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material.
paras.zh: 首先，学生缺乏学习的愿望，他们只是为了以及格的成绩拿到学分而完成作业，而不是真正投入地学习课程内容。

paras.en: As online courses tend to have more than 100 students, most of the assignments are short and simple.
paras.zh: 由于网络课程的学生往往超过100人，大部分作业都简短而容易。

paras.en: They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students.
paras.zh: 这些作业的设计目的不是让学生与课程内容深入互动，而是便于评分，以适应如此庞大的学生人数。

w.m: v. 设计；（为某目的）打造
v. 适应；顾及；满足……的需要

paras.en: Perhaps the biggest disadvantage of taking an online class is the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students.
paras.zh: 修读网络课程最大的弊端，或许在于老师和学生之间缺少面对面的互动。

paras.en: Live sessions are infrequent and are often scheduled during the middle of the day when students have to attend other classes or work.
paras.zh: 直播课次数很少，而且常常安排在中午前后，而这个时候学生得去上别的课或者去上班。

w.m: adj. 现场直播的；实时的
adj. 不常发生的；稀少的

paras.en: The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times for many students.
paras.zh: 教授的答疑时间也可能正好是许多学生不方便的时候。

paras.en: Most interaction with the professor has to be through email, which is often impersonal.
paras.zh: 与教授的互动大多只能借助电子邮件，而电子邮件往往缺乏人情味。

w.m: adj. 缺乏人情味的；冷淡的

paras.en: It is nearly impossible for students to build a relationship with their professor.
paras.zh: 学生几乎不可能与教授建立起关系。

paras.en: There is also little interaction amongst students.
paras.zh: 学生之间的互动也很少。

w.m: adj. 很少的；几乎没有的

paras.en: It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers.
paras.zh: 对学生来说，组建学习小组、与同学建立关系可能会更难。

w.m: n. 同龄人；同伴（此处指同学）

paras.en: Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection.
paras.zh: 网络课程还需要一台电脑或笔记本电脑，以及稳定的网络连接。

paras.en: Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage.
paras.zh: 无论是出于经济原因还是其他原因，并非所有学生都能用上这类资源，有些学生可能会处于不利地位。

paras.en: Offering online classes certainly helps students who would otherwise not be able to attend classroom sessions.
paras.zh: 开设网络课程无疑能帮助那些原本无法到教室上课的学生。

w.m: adv. 否则；不然的话；在其他情况下

paras.en: However, online classes fail to provide a genuine education, with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking.
paras.zh: 然而，网络课程未能提供真正的教育，注重的是便利，而不是批判性思维。

paras.en: We need restructured online classes in which students can have a learning experience that will actually provide quality education.
paras.zh: 我们需要经过重构的网络课程，让学生能在其中获得真正提供优质教育的学习体验。

w.m: adj. 经过重构的；重组的

passages.name: 2022年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 让科学辩论公开透明
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科学与社会
passages.summary: 在互联网时代，不存在私下的辩论，一些科学家对此有所顾虑。文章认为，辩论走出大学和政府机构后，信息有可能遭到错误使用，造成公众困惑，但公开辩论也能促进科学界与公众的交流，引起公众更多的关注，并鼓励更加多元的声音。有专家担心，公开的推测可能让人们认为细节上的分歧意味着科学界对现代药物的安全性和有效性缺乏足够的共识，作者认为这种担忧似乎是多余的：去参加会议、辩论科学问题的日子已经一去不复返，这是好事，因为那些聚会不够多元，把许多重要的声音排除在外。作者主张让科学辩论透明而热烈，并指出，要让公众明白科学是一个自我纠错的过程，就需要摒弃“科学是教科书里一套固定不变的事实”这一观念。

paras.en: In the age of the internet, there’s no such thing as a private debate.
paras.zh: 在互联网时代，不存在私下辩论这回事。

w.m: 根本没有……这回事；不存在……

paras.en: But is that bad for science?
paras.zh: 但这对科学不利吗？

paras.en: Some scientists have had concerns.
paras.zh: 一些科学家一直心存顾虑。

paras.en: When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there’s potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public.
paras.zh: 任何领域的辩论一旦走出大学和政府机构的殿堂，信息就有可能遭到错误使用，从而造成公众困惑；然而，公开辩论也能促进科学界与公众之间的交流。

paras.en: Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices.
paras.zh: 最近围绕科学研究、健康和政策展开的公开辩论引起了公众更多的关注，也鼓励了更加多元的声音。

paras.en: If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems—and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly—then this is good for everyone, including scientists.
paras.zh: 如果这一趋势促使科学家更快地就我们所面临问题的最佳解决办法达成一致，同时又帮助公众更清楚地观察科学讨论的过程，那么这对包括科学家在内的所有人都有好处。

paras.en: A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced.
paras.zh: 《纽约时报》最近刊登的一场辩论探讨了药物应该以多快的速度研发和生产的问题。

paras.en: Issues such as the safety of the product and the perception of the public were examined and considered.
paras.zh: 诸如产品的安全性、公众的看法等问题得到了审视和考量。

paras.en: But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficacy of modern-day medicine.
paras.zh: 但一些专家担心，这种公开的推测可能会让人们认为，在细节上存在分歧，就意味着对现代药物的安全性和有效性缺乏足够的科学共识。

paras.en: The anxiety seems misplaced.
paras.zh: 这种担忧似乎是多余的。

w.m: adj. （担忧、信任等）不恰当的；不必要的

paras.en: Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that’s good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices.
paras.zh: 去参加会议、辩论科学问题的日子已经一去不复返了，这是好事，因为那些聚会不够多元，把许多重要的声音排除在外。

paras.en: These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place.
paras.zh: 如今，有关科学的辩论无论在哪里进行，公众都能接触到。

paras.en: For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules, but rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held.
paras.zh: 对许多科学家来说，公开辩论是一个新领域，可能让人感觉像是一个几乎没有约束或规则的地方；但与其回避这类对话，不如让这些辩论透明而热烈，无论在哪里举行。

w.m: adj. 热烈的；充满活力的

paras.en: If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed.
paras.zh: 如果要让公众明白科学是一个可敬的自我纠错过程，就需要摒弃这样一种观念：科学是教科书里一套固定不变的事实。

w.m: adj. 自我纠正的；自我纠错的

paras.en: With the validity of science coming under attack, there’s a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life.
paras.zh: 在科学的正确性正遭受攻击之际，有必要让人们把科学辩论看作是公开的、真实的。

paras.en: Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all.
paras.zh: 让每个人都看到那些喧闹而杂乱的商讨吧，它们推动科学进步，带来对我们所有人都有益的决定。

passages.name: 2022年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 社交媒体的隐患：留不住员工
passages.genre: 议论文 · 职场与管理
passages.summary: 许多员工认为社交媒体有助于改善工作关系、为决策提供支持，雇主却通常担心它会扼杀工作效率。作者对一家医疗保健机构的277名员工开展研究后发现，这种担忧是错误的：社交媒体降低工作效率的程度，远不及它在留住员工方面造成的破坏——在工作中使用社交媒体的员工更投入、效率更高，但也更有可能离职。作者因此建议管理者采取措施抵消这一风险，例如建立社交媒体群组来促进员工协作，并借助社交媒体表彰员工的成就、展示他们的成功事迹，以直接降低跳槽意向。

paras.en: Social media can be a powerful communication tool for employees, helping them to collaborate, share ideas and solve problems.
paras.zh: 对员工来说，社交媒体可以成为一种强大的沟通工具，帮助他们协作、分享想法和解决问题。

paras.en: Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes.
paras.zh: 研究表明，82%的员工认为社交媒体能够改善工作关系，60%的员工相信它能够为决策过程提供支持。

paras.en: These beliefs contribute to a majority of workers connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours.
paras.zh: 这些看法促使大多数员工在社交媒体上与同事联系，甚至在工作时间也是如此。

w.m: 促使；促成；是……的原因之一

paras.en: Employers typically worry that social media is a productivity killer; more than half of U.S. employers reportedly block access to social media at work.
paras.zh: 雇主通常担心社交媒体是工作效率的杀手；据报道，美国一半以上的雇主在工作场所禁止访问社交媒体。

paras.en: In my research with 277 employees of a healthcare organization I found these concerns to be misguided.
paras.zh: 我以一家医疗保健机构的277名员工为对象开展研究，发现这些担忧是错误的。

w.m: adj. 判断失误的；错误的

paras.en: Social media doesn’t reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention.
paras.zh: 社交媒体虽然会降低工作效率，但远不及它在留住员工方面造成的破坏那么严重。

paras.en: In the first part of the study I surveyed the employees about why and how they used platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn.
paras.zh: 在研究的第一部分，我调查了员工为什么以及如何使用Facebook、Twitter或LinkedIn这类平台。

w.m: v. （就某事）调查；对……做问卷调查

paras.en: Respondents were then asked about their work behaviors, including whether they felt motivated in their jobs and showed initiative at work.
paras.zh: 随后，受访者被问及自己的工作行为，包括是否对工作有干劲，以及是否在工作中表现出主动性。

w.m: adj. 有干劲的；积极性高的
表现出主动性；积极主动

paras.en: I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas.
paras.zh: 我发现，通过社交媒体博客与同事开展线上社交互动的员工，往往更有干劲，并会提出创新的想法。

w.m: adj. 有干劲的；积极性高的

paras.en: But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative.
paras.zh: 但员工如果与机构以外的人互动，干劲就会更小，表现出的主动性也更少。

w.m: adj. 有干劲的；积极性高的
表现出主动性；积极主动

paras.en: In the second part of the study I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media.
paras.zh: 在研究的第二部分，我发现，为工作而使用社交媒体的员工中，有76%对自己在社交媒体上看到的其他机构产生了兴趣。

paras.en: When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections.
paras.zh: 我考察了受访者如何表现出对新职业和新雇主的开放态度，发现他们会从事一些关键活动，包括调研新的机构、建立新的工作人脉。

w.m: 对……持开放态度；乐于接受
n. 人脉；（工作上的）关系

paras.en: These findings present a dilemma for managers: employees using social media at work are more engaged and more productive, but they are also more likely to leave your company.
paras.zh: 这些发现给管理者出了一道难题：在工作中使用社交媒体的员工投入度更高、效率也更高，但他们离开你公司的可能性也更大。

w.m: adj. 投入的；全身心参与的
adj. 效率高的；富有成效的

paras.en: Managers should implement solutions that neutralize the retention risk caused by social media.
paras.zh: 管理者应当实施一些解决方案，抵消社交媒体给留住员工带来的风险。

w.m: n. 解决方案；解决办法

paras.en: They can create social media groups in which employees will be more likely to collaborate and less likely to share withdrawal intentions or discussions about external job opportunities.
paras.zh: 他们可以建立社交媒体群组，在这些群组里，员工协作的可能性会更大，而透露离职意向或谈论外部工作机会的可能性则会更小。

paras.en: Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover (跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees’ accomplishments and giving visibility to employees’ success stories.
paras.zh: 管理者还可以利用社交媒体，通过表彰员工的成就、展示员工的成功事迹，直接降低员工的跳槽意向。

passages.name: 2022年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 远程教育比不上传统课堂
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与科技
passages.summary: 削减教育预算的时代即将到来，远程学习可能会成为常态，主管教育预算的人可能受到把教师换成技术的诱惑。作者认为，告别由活生生的人每天授课、与学生互动的传统课堂将是一场灾难：亲身到校上学有隐性的好处，学校还提供餐食、辅导等支持，而远程教育永远比不上传统课堂中的面对面教学。作者主张学校不应永久“远程化”，技术只应是好老师的工具。

paras.en: In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm.
paras.zh: 削减教育预算的时代即将到来，届时远程学习可能会成为常态。

paras.en: The temptation for those in charge of education budgets to trade teachers for technology could be so strong that they ignore the disadvantages of distance learning.
paras.zh: 对主管教育预算的人来说，把教师换成技术的诱惑可能强烈到让他们忽视远程学习的弊端。

paras.en: School facilities are expensive to build and maintain, and teachers are expensive to employ.
paras.zh: 学校设施的建造和维护费用高昂，聘用教师的开支也很大。

paras.en: Online classes do not require buildings, and each class can host hundreds of people simultaneously, resulting in greater savings, thus increasing the temptation of distance education for those concerned more about budgets than learning.
paras.zh: 网课不需要校舍，而且每堂课都能同时容纳数百人，因而能省下更多开支，这就让远程教育对那些更关心预算而不是学习的人更具诱惑力。

w.m: n. 节省；节约下来的钱

paras.en: But moving away from a traditional classroom in which a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students daily would be a disaster.
paras.zh: 但在传统课堂上，一个活生生的人每天给学生上课、与他们互动，告别这样的课堂将会是一场灾难。

paras.en: Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people.
paras.zh: 亲身到校上学有隐性的好处：每天早起、与同龄人互动、与老师建立关系，都是需要在年轻人身上培养的必备技能。

w.m: adj. 隐藏的；不易察觉的
adj. 必不可少的；必备的

paras.en: Moreover, schools should be more than simple institutions of traditional learning.
paras.zh: 此外，学校应当不只是单纯的传统学习机构。

paras.en: They are now places that provide meals.
paras.zh: 如今，学校是提供餐食的地方。

paras.en: They are places where students receive counseling and other support.
paras.zh: 学校也是学生接受辅导和其他支持的地方。

paras.en: Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to “transform” education overnight.
paras.zh: 那些政策制定者常常迷恋教育领域的最新技术，以及它在一夜之间“变革”教育的潜力。

paras.en: But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help.
paras.zh: 但网络教育无法让老师在课后留下学习吃力的学生，为他们提供帮助。

w.m: adj. 学习吃力的；处境艰难的

paras.en: Educational videos may deliver academic content, but they are unable to make eye contact or assess a student’s level of engagement.
paras.zh: 教学视频或许能传授学业内容，却无法和学生眼神交流，也无法评估学生的投入程度。

w.m: adj. 教育的；有教育意义的

paras.en: Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom.
paras.zh: 远程教育永远比不上传统课堂中的面对面教学。

paras.en: In their first 18 years of life, American children spend only 9% of their time in school.
paras.zh: 在人生的头18年里，美国孩子只有9%的时间在学校度过。

paras.en: Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market.
paras.zh: 然而，人们却期望老师让孩子们做好成为负责任公民的准备，培养他们的社交技能，鼓励他们管理好时间，并增强他们在日益严酷的劳动力市场中茁壮成长的能力。

paras.en: Given these expectations, schools should not become permanently “remote”.
paras.zh: 考虑到这些期望，学校不应该永久“远程化”。

paras.en: The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time.
paras.zh: 课堂的力量根植于同一时间、同一地点相聚的人们所具有的人性。

paras.en: Personal teaching is about teachers showing students a higher path, and about young people going through the process together.
paras.zh: 面对面教学的要义，在于老师为学生指明一条更高远的道路，也在于年轻人一起经历这个过程。

paras.en: Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher.
paras.zh: 技术无论多么先进，都只应该是好老师的工具。

passages.name: 2022年12月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 健康国家的饮食与生活习惯
passages.genre: 说明文 · 饮食与健康
passages.summary: 营养学家哈利·帕斯特纳克为写书走访了世界各地最健康的国家，发现北美的生活方式与许多其他国家很不一样：美国人吃的分量大得多，也不优先考虑吃应季或本地的食物，还往食物里添加大量的盐、糖和增稠剂。相比之下，地中海饮食等健康饮食似乎都保持着以本地区应季农产品为本的特质，其他大多数健康饮食文化也把吃饭当成一件大事。帕斯特纳克还注意到，这些健康国家中的大多数唯一共有的特点是，那里的人走路比普通美国人多得多。

paras.en: To write his 2010 book, The 5-Factor World Diet, nutritionist Harley Pasternak traveled to the healthiest countries around the world to learn more about what made their meals extra nourishing.
paras.zh: 为了写作2010年出版的《5因素世界饮食》一书，营养学家哈利·帕斯特纳克走访了世界各地最健康的国家，想进一步了解是什么让这些国家的饭菜格外有营养。

paras.en: He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal.
paras.zh: 他注意到，日本人吃的海藻种类之多令人赞叹，而中国人则力求每顿饭都至少包含五种不同的颜色。

w.m: adj. 极好的；令人赞叹的
各种各样的；多种多样的

paras.en: Pasternak also came away with some valuable observations about how different the North American way of life was, compared with that of many other countries.
paras.zh: 关于北美的生活方式与许多其他国家相比有多么不同，帕斯特纳克还带回了一些宝贵的观察心得。

w.m: 带着（收获、印象等）离开；获得

paras.en: For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries.
paras.zh: 首先，美国人吃的分量比其他国家的人大得多。

paras.en: “We don’t prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods,” explained Pasternak.
paras.zh: “我们不优先考虑吃应季或本地的食物，还往食物里添加大量的盐、糖和增稠剂，”帕斯特纳克解释说。

w.m: v. 优先考虑；把……放在首位

paras.en: Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak’s book.
paras.zh: 把这种情况与帕斯特纳克书中列出的健康的地中海饮食、北欧饮食和冲绳饮食对比一下。

paras.en: They all seem to stick to the ethos (特质) of regional, seasonal produce.
paras.zh: 这些饮食似乎都保持着以本地区应季农产品为本的特质。

paras.en: For example, a traditional Mediterranean diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and olive oil as the main components of nutritional intake.
paras.zh: 例如，传统的地中海饮食包括水果、蔬菜、全谷物、坚果和橄榄油，以它们作为营养摄入的主要组成部分。

paras.en: Fish, chicken and red wine make moderate appearances, while red meat, salt and sugar are used much less often.
paras.zh: 鱼、鸡肉和红酒出现的频率适中，而红肉、盐和糖的使用频率则低得多。

paras.en: The benefits of a traditional Mediterranean diet have been studied since the 1970s, and researchers have found that living that olive oil life can help people lose weight, lower their heart disease risk and reverse diabetes.
paras.zh: 自20世纪70年代以来，人们一直在研究传统地中海饮食的益处；研究人员发现，过这种橄榄油式的生活能帮助人们减轻体重、降低患心脏病的风险并逆转糖尿病。

paras.en: Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event—say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch—as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal over the kitchen sink and calling it dinner.
paras.zh: 其他大多数健康饮食文化也把吃饭当成一件大事，比如一家人围着餐桌吃上好几道菜，或是吃一顿长长的午餐，配上一两杯红酒，而不是对着厨房水槽匆匆狼吞虎咽几把麦片，就当是吃了晚饭。

paras.en: Each of the healthy eating cultures has its own unique feature.
paras.zh: 每种健康饮食文化都有自己独特的特点。

w.m: adj. 独特的；独一无二的

paras.en: But Pasternak did take note of one unifying factor in most of the healthy societies he observed.
paras.zh: 不过，帕斯特纳克确实注意到，在他观察过的大多数健康社会里，存在着一个共同因素。

paras.en: “The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American,” said Pasternak.
paras.zh: “这些健康国家中的大多数，唯一共有的特点就是那里的人走路都比普通美国人多得多，”帕斯特纳克说。

paras.en: “So really, regardless of what you’re eating, if someone’s walking four miles more than you each day, they’re going to be a lot thinner and live a lot longer than you.”
paras.zh: “所以说真的，不管你吃的是什么，如果有人每天比你多走四英里，那他就会比你瘦得多，也会比你长寿得多。”

passages.name: 2022年12月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 情商高也可能带来压力
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与情绪
passages.summary: 一项新研究表明，对他人的情绪敏感，有时可能会带来一份额外的压力；这项研究和其他研究都对“情商对其拥有者一概有益”这一主流观点提出了质疑。实验中，被评定为情商更高的男大学生在表情严肃的评委面前做求职演讲时，压力指标升得更多，回落到基线水平所需的时间也更长。研究者贝希托尔特认为，情商仍是一项有用的技能，但前提是要学会妥善应对他人和自己的情绪。

paras.en: Recognizing when a friend or colleague feels sad, angry or surprised is key to getting along with others.
paras.zh: 识别出朋友或同事何时感到悲伤、愤怒或惊讶，是与他人和睦相处的关键。

paras.en: But a new study suggests that being sensitive to people’s feelings may sometimes come with an extra dose of stress.
paras.zh: 但一项新研究表明，对他人的情绪敏感，有时可能会带来一份额外的压力。

paras.en: This and other research challenge the prevailing view that emotional intelligence is uniformly beneficial to its bearer.
paras.zh: 这项研究和其他研究都对一种主流观点提出了质疑，即情商对其拥有者一概有益。

paras.en: In a study, psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt of the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management in Germany and her colleague asked 166 male university students a series of questions to measure their emotional intelligence.
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，德国法兰克福金融管理学院的心理学家米丽亚姆·贝希托尔特和她的一位同事向166名男大学生提出了一系列问题，以测量他们的情商。

paras.en: For example, they showed the students photographs of people’s faces and asked them to what extent feelings such as happiness or disgust were being expressed.
paras.zh: 例如，他们给学生们看人脸照片，并问他们这些面孔在多大程度上流露出快乐或厌恶之类的情绪。

paras.en: The students then had to give job talks in front of judges who displayed serious facial expressions.
paras.zh: 随后，学生们必须在面带严肃表情的评委面前做求职演讲。

paras.en: The scientists measured concentrations of stress hormones in the students’ saliva (唾液) before and after the talk.
paras.zh: 科学家们在演讲前后测量了学生唾液中压力激素的浓度。

paras.en: In students who were rated more emotionally intelligent, the stress measures increased more during the experiment and took longer to go back to baseline.
paras.zh: 在被评定为情商更高的学生身上，压力指标在实验过程中升得更多，回落到基线水平所需的时间也更长。

paras.en: The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good, says Bechtoldt.
paras.zh: 贝希托尔特说，研究结果表明，有些人在情绪方面可能过于聪明，反而对自己不利。

paras.en: “Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble,” she notes.
paras.zh: “有时候，你可能在某件事上太过擅长，以至于惹出麻烦，”她指出。

paras.en: Indeed, the study adds to previous research hinting at a dark side of emotional intelligence.
paras.zh: 的确，这项研究是对以往研究的补充，那些研究暗示情商存在阴暗的一面。

paras.en: A study published in 2002 in Personality and Individual Differences suggested that emotionally perceptive people might be particularly influenced by feelings of depression and hopelessness.
paras.zh: 2002年发表在《人格与个体差异》上的一项研究表明，善于察觉情绪的人受抑郁和绝望情绪的影响可能尤其大。

w.m: adj. 感知敏锐的；有洞察力的

paras.en: Furthermore, several studies have implied that emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gain.
paras.zh: 此外，已有几项研究暗示，情商可以用来操纵他人，以谋取私利。

paras.en: More research is needed to see how exactly the relation between emotional intelligence and stress would play out in women and in people of different ages and education levels.
paras.zh: 还需要更多研究，才能弄清情商与压力之间的关系在女性以及不同年龄和受教育程度的人身上究竟会如何体现。

paras.en: Nevertheless, emotional intelligence is a useful skill to have, as long as you learn to also properly cope with emotions—both others’ and your own, says Bechtoldt.
paras.zh: 贝希托尔特说，尽管如此，情商仍是一项有用的技能，只要你同时学会妥善应对情绪——既包括他人的情绪，也包括你自己的情绪。

paras.en: For example, some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people’s sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out.
paras.zh: 例如，一些敏感的人可能会为别人的悲伤或愤怒承担起责任，而这最终会让他们压力重重。

paras.en: Remember, as Bechtoldt says, “you are not responsible for how other people feel.”
paras.zh: 请记住，正如贝希托尔特所说，“你无须为别人的感受负责。”

passages.name: 2022年12月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 水产养殖的兴起与隐忧
passages.genre: 说明文 · 食品与环境
passages.summary: 如今人类吃的鱼比以往任何时候都多，而且人类历史上第一次，我们的水产食品大部分来自养殖，而非捕捞。由于野外捕捞的鱼量自20世纪90年代以来已趋于平稳，要按目前的速度继续吃鱼，就需要让水产养殖持续发展；目前，超过十分之三的海洋鱼类种群已遭过度捕捞。文章指出，转向水产养殖对保障粮食安全和可持续性至关重要，因为饲养牛、猪等陆生动物需要大量的谷物和水；但水产养殖并非万全之策，在一些东南亚国家，养虾业就对海洋生态系统造成灾难性的破坏。

paras.en: We’re eating more fish than ever these days.
paras.zh: 如今，我们吃的鱼比以往任何时候都多。

paras.en: At around 20 kilograms per person, global fish consumption is now more than twice what it was in the 1960s.
paras.zh: 全球鱼类消费量现已达到人均约20千克，是20世纪60年代的两倍多。

paras.en: What’s really remarkable, though, is where that fish comes from.
paras.zh: 不过，真正引人注目的是这些鱼从哪里来。

w.m: adj. 引人注目的；非同寻常的

paras.en: For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic (水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing.
paras.zh: 如今，我们的水产食品大部分来自养殖，而非捕捞，这在人类历史上尚属首次。

paras.en: People ate around 73 million tonnes of farmed fish—just more than half of the volume of fish that humans consumed—in 2014.
paras.zh: 2014年，人们吃掉了约7300万吨养殖鱼，略多于人类当年鱼类消费总量的一半。

paras.en: That’s out of a total fish supply of 167 million tonnes; the remaining 20 million or so tonnes go into things like animal feed and medical products.
paras.zh: 人类消费的这些鱼，出自1.67亿吨的鱼类总供应量；其余2000万吨左右则用来制作动物饲料、医疗产品等。

paras.en: To keep eating fish at the current rate, we’re definitely going to need to keep aquaculture (水产养殖) developing.
paras.zh: 要按目前的速度继续吃鱼，我们肯定需要让水产养殖持续发展。

paras.en: That’s because the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s.
paras.zh: 这是因为自20世纪90年代以来，野外捕捞的鱼量就已趋于平稳。

paras.en: Back in 1974, only 10% of marine fish stocks had been overfished.
paras.zh: 1974年时，只有10%的海洋鱼类种群遭到了过度捕捞。

paras.en: Now, more than three-tenths are.
paras.zh: 如今，这一比例已超过十分之三。

paras.en: Only a tenth of our oceans’ fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels.
paras.zh: 我们海洋中的鱼类种群只有十分之一能承受比目前水平更大的捕捞强度。

paras.en: But while catches at sea have suffered, fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate.
paras.zh: 但是，尽管海上捕捞量受到了冲击，鱼类养殖却一直在快速增长。

paras.en: A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world’s farmed fish.
paras.zh: 这一增长很大一部分来自中国，中国的养殖鱼产量占全世界的60%。

paras.en: In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish.
paras.zh: 事实上，包括中国在内，如今约有35个国家生产的养殖鱼多于野生捕捞的鱼。

paras.en: This shift toward aquaculture isn’t just good for ensuring salmon (三文鱼) on your plate; it’s also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability.
paras.zh: 这种向水产养殖的转变不仅有利于确保你的餐盘里有三文鱼，对保障粮食安全和可持续性也至关重要。

paras.en: By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people.
paras.zh: 到2050年，世界需要养活的人口估计将达到97亿。

paras.en: They’ll have to get their protein somewhere.
paras.zh: 他们总得从某个地方获取蛋白质。

paras.en: However, raising cattle, pigs, and other land-based animals requires vast amounts of grain and water.
paras.zh: 然而，饲养牛、猪等陆生动物需要大量的谷物和水。

paras.en: For example, pound for pound, beef requires 15 times more feed to raise than carp, a freshwater fish farmed all over Asia.
paras.zh: 例如，养出同等重量的牛肉和鲤鱼，前者所需的饲料是后者的15倍；鲤鱼是一种在亚洲各地都有养殖的淡水鱼。

paras.en: That grain—and the water needed to grow it—could be consumed by people instead.
paras.zh: 这些谷物，连同种植谷物所需的水，本可以转而供人类消费。

paras.en: However, aquaculture is no silver bullet.
paras.zh: 然而，水产养殖并非万全之策。

paras.en: In some Southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems.
paras.zh: 在一些东南亚国家，养虾业对海洋生态系统造成灾难性的破坏。

paras.en: Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular seafoods worldwide.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管存在这些问题，虾仍然是全世界最受欢迎的海鲜之一。

passages.name: 2022年12月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 世界粮食计划署为何获和平奖
passages.genre: 议论文 · 粮食与全球发展
passages.summary: 2020年诺贝尔和平奖授予了世界粮食计划署，对那些从生存边缘跌落的人来说，它就是安全网；尽管消除饥饿的努力已持续数十年，地球上仍有约11%的人每天都在忍受营养不良，减少营养不良的进展也已停滞。发达国家有时向发展中国家提供粮食和援助，但这是有代价的；附带苛刻条件的援助往往会扩大贫富差距，正因如此，该署的工作才如此重要。作者认为，科学界可以向该署伸出援手：科学家可以与最易陷入贫困和饥饿的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识；一些最贫穷国家战胜粮食短缺的能力不会来自富裕国家的贷款或世界经济机构，而将建立在充满自信的人们运用开放、共享的科学知识摆脱苦难的基础上。

paras.en: In 2020, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP).
paras.zh: 2020年，诺贝尔和平奖授予了世界粮食计划署（WFP）。

w.m: 世界粮食计划署（联合国机构）

paras.en: Why a Nobel Prize for the WFP, and why now?
paras.zh: 诺贝尔奖为何颁给世界粮食计划署？又为何是现在？

paras.en: In 2019, the WFP assisted nearly 100 million people in 88 countries.
paras.zh: 2019年，世界粮食计划署为88个国家的近1亿人提供了援助。

paras.en: It is the safety net for those who fall off the edge of existence.
paras.zh: 对那些从生存边缘跌落的人来说，它就是安全网。

paras.en: It is a response to the problem of food instability.
paras.zh: 它是应对粮食不稳定问题的一种举措。

paras.en: Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else’s problem.
paras.zh: 它荣获诺贝尔奖，提醒我们所有人：以为穷人和弱势群体是别人的问题，这种想法隐含着道德风险。

w.m: v. 设想；（想当然地）以为
穷人（the+形容词表示一类人）
adj. 弱势的；（the vulnerable）弱势群体
别人的问题；与己无关的事

paras.en: The WFP has been around since 1961 and has been the global coordinator of nationally based efforts to avoid disasters with food aid.
paras.zh: 世界粮食计划署自1961年就已存在，一直是全球协调者，负责协调各国借助粮食援助避免灾难的行动。

w.m: 以国家为单位的；在各国层面开展的

paras.en: Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment.
paras.zh: 尽管消除饥饿的努力已持续了数十年，但据最新估计，地球上约11%的人（约8.2亿人）每天都在忍受营养不良。

paras.en: Progress in reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s.
paras.zh: 尽管整个20世纪90年代和21世纪头十年都曾取得成效，但减少营养不良的进展已经停滞。

paras.en: Developed countries sometimes offer food and aid to developing ones, but at a price.
paras.zh: 发达国家有时会向发展中国家提供粮食和援助，但这是有代价的。

paras.en: One American philosopher stated that addressing the needs of the poor and vulnerable is about more than money—it is mostly about creating conditions under which prosperity and opportunity can thrive.
paras.zh: 一位美国哲学家曾表示，满足穷人和弱势群体的需求不只关乎金钱——它主要在于创造条件，让繁荣和机遇得以蓬勃发展。

w.m: v. 设法解决；满足（需求）
穷人（the+形容词表示一类人）
adj. 弱势的；（the vulnerable）弱势群体
在其中；在这种（条件）下（介词+which引导定语从句）

paras.en: When aid is offered with heavy conditions attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order.
paras.zh: 如果提供援助时附带苛刻的条件，比如偿还贷款或以资源换粮食，这种援助往往会扩大贫富差距，维系旧的世界秩序。

paras.en: This is why the work of the WFP is so vital.
paras.zh: 正因如此，世界粮食计划署的工作才如此重要。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此
adj. 至关重要的；必不可少的

paras.en: The scientific community, however, can provide a helping hand to the WFP.
paras.zh: 不过，科学界可以向世界粮食计划署伸出援手。

paras.en: By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems.
paras.zh: 通过与那些最易陷入贫困和饥饿的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识，科学家能够帮助减轻这些问题。

w.m: n. 同行；同等地位的人

paras.en: By making its voice heard, science can lead by example.
paras.zh: 通过发出自己的声音，科学可以以身作则。

w.m: 发出自己的声音；让别人听到自己的意见

paras.en: The ability to overcome food shortages that must be built into some of the poorest countries will not come from loans from wealthy countries, which may have food problems of their own, or world economic institutions.
paras.zh: 一些最贫穷的国家必须建立起战胜粮食短缺的能力，而这种能力既不会来自富裕国家的贷款——它们自身可能也存在粮食问题——也不会来自世界经济机构。

paras.en: This ability will be built upon self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge to pull themselves out of their misery.
paras.zh: 这种能力将建立在这样的基础上：充满自信的人们运用开放、共享的科学知识，让自己摆脱苦难。

passages.name: 2022年12月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 改变养老院的托马斯医生
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与养老
passages.summary: 在人们把变老看作不可避免的痛苦的时代，比尔·托马斯医生过去25年来一直在为老年人改变游戏规则。1991年他调任纽约州北部一家养老院的医疗主任后，冒险把动物和植物引进养老院，结果医疗处方减少了50%，死亡率大幅下降，入住老人也更快乐了。他的方法名为“伊甸园替代模式”，促使养老院给予老人更自主、更有创造性的生活空间，已在多个国家得到采用并取得巨大成功；他还一直宣扬变老并不是一件坏事。

paras.en: Even though we are living in an age where growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery, this doctor has been changing the game for seniors over the last 25 years.
paras.zh: 尽管在我们所处的这个时代，人们把变老看作一种不可避免的痛苦，但过去25年来，这位医生一直在为老年人改变游戏规则。

w.m: 改变游戏规则；彻底改变局面

paras.en: It all started in 1991 when the Harvard-educated physician was transferred from working in a stressful emergency room to being the medical director of a nursing home in upstate New York.
paras.zh: 这一切始于1991年，那一年，这位哈佛出身的医生从压力很大的急诊室调到纽约州北部的一家养老院，担任医疗主任。

w.m: adj. 哈佛出身的；在哈佛受过教育的

paras.en: The depressing and regimented (严格管制的) environment got him thinking about what exactly could improve the residents’ conditions.
paras.zh: 那里令人压抑、管制严格的环境让他开始思考：究竟什么能够改善入住老人的状况。

w.m: adj. 令人压抑的；令人沮丧的

paras.en: Even though animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time, Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance.
paras.zh: 尽管当时在养老院里养动物是违法的，比尔·托马斯医生还是冒险一试。

paras.en: Acting on a hunch (直觉), he brought in two dogs, four cats, hens, rabbits, 100 birds, a multitude of plants, a flower garden, and a vegetable patch.
paras.zh: 他凭直觉行事，引进了两条狗、四只猫、一些母鸡和兔子、100只鸟以及大量植物，还开辟了一座花园和一块菜地。

paras.en: The change was dramatic.
paras.zh: 变化非常显著。

paras.en: There was a 50% drop in medical prescriptions along with a dramatic decrease in death rates—but most importantly, the residents were simply happier.
paras.zh: 医疗处方减少了50%，同时死亡率大幅下降，但最重要的是，入住老人就是比以前快乐了。

paras.en: Dr. Thomas’s approach, named the Eden Alternative, has driven nursing homes to allow a more autonomous (自主的) and creative living space for their elderly.
paras.zh: 托马斯医生的方法名为“伊甸园替代模式”，它已促使养老院给予院内老人更自主、更有创造性的生活空间。

w.m: n. 替代方案；另一种选择
n. 老年人（与 the 或物主代词连用）

paras.en: It erases the belief that growing old means growing useless.
paras.zh: 它消除了这样一种观念：变老就意味着变得无用。

paras.en: He encourages residents to think of their age as an enriching new phase of life rather than the end of it.
paras.zh: 他鼓励入住老人把自己的年纪看作人生中一个令人充实的新阶段，而不是人生的终点。

w.m: adj. 使人充实的；丰富人生的

paras.en: Thomas, now a speaker and author of several books, also created small, independently run residences with their own bedrooms and bathrooms, and he has been preaching a singular message that getting old is not a bad thing.
paras.zh: 托马斯如今是一名演说家，也是好几本书的作者。他还创办了一些独立运营的小型住所，里面配有独立的卧室和浴室；他一直在宣扬的只有一个理念：变老并不是一件坏事。

w.m: n. 理念；要传达的信息

paras.en: “Within six weeks, they had to send a truck around to pick up all the wheelchairs,” Thomas told the Washington Post.
paras.zh: “六周之内，他们就不得不派一辆卡车过来，把所有轮椅都收走，”托马斯对《华盛顿邮报》说。

paras.en: “You know why most people in nursing homes use wheelchairs?
paras.zh: “你知道养老院里的大多数人为什么坐轮椅吗？

paras.en: Because the buildings are so big.”
paras.zh: 因为那些楼太大了。”

paras.en: The 56-year-old doctor’s methods have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America with enormous success.
paras.zh: 这位56岁医生的方法已在澳大利亚、日本、加拿大和美国得到采用，并取得了巨大成功。

paras.en: Last year he published Second Wind: Navigating the Passage to a Slower, Deeper, and More Connected Life, a guide on how to shift our perspectives on aging and growth.
paras.zh: 去年，他出版了《重振活力：顺利过渡到更慢、更深、联系更紧密的人生》，这本指南讲的是如何转变我们对衰老和成长的看法。

w.m: 重新振作的力量；恢复的元气

paras.en: He is currently traveling through North America performing with his guitar and his enthusiasm on his Age of Disruption Tour.
paras.zh: 他目前正在北美各地游历，在他的“颠覆时代”巡回演出中带着吉他、满怀热情地表演。

passages.name: 2022年12月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 饮食质量为何因社会阶层而异
passages.genre: 议论文 · 健康与社会
passages.summary: 研究表明，在发达国家，较富裕、受教育程度较高的人往往摄入质量更高的饮食，而经济上处于弱势的人所报告的饮食营养贫乏、能量密度高，低收入人群的肥胖率和糖尿病发病率也往往更高，但研究并未解释其中的原因。促进健康饮食的公共卫生举措常常侧重营养教育，预先假定低收入人群食物素养较低；然而研究表明，食物无保障家庭的成年人在调整食谱和烹饪技能方面并不逊色，弱势群体受制于自身的经济、物质和社会状况，低收入家庭也称食物价格是他们改善饮食的障碍。不过，虽然质量较高的饮食通常更贵，但这本身并不能证明健康饮食必然更贵或贵得令人望而却步：毕竟并非所有社会经济地位处于弱势的人都吃得很差，而且我们很容易就能想到不少既便宜又有营养的食物和食谱。

paras.en: Research shows that in developed countries, more affluent and educated people tend to consume higher-quality diets—including more fruits and vegetables, fish and whole grains.
paras.zh: 研究表明，在发达国家，较富裕、受教育程度较高的人往往摄入质量更高的饮食，包括更多的水果和蔬菜、鱼类以及全谷物。

paras.en: In contrast, economically disadvantaged people report diets that are nutrient-poor and energy-dense.
paras.zh: 相比之下，经济上处于弱势的人所报告的饮食营养贫乏、能量密度高。

w.m: adj. 处于弱势的；贫困的
v. 报告；（在调查中）自述

paras.en: They are less likely to have food-purchasing habits that conform to public health recommendations.
paras.zh: 他们的食物购买习惯符合公共卫生建议的可能性更小。

paras.en: These dietary differences are often accompanied by higher rates of obesity and diabetes among lower-income people.
paras.zh: 这些饮食差异往往伴随着低收入人群中更高的肥胖率和糖尿病发病率。

w.m: adj. 低收入的；收入较低的

paras.en: This relationship between social class and diet quality and health is extensively documented.
paras.zh: 社会阶层与饮食质量和健康之间的这种关系，已有大量文献记载。

paras.en: However, the research does not explain why this is the case—a question that has significant implications for designing effective policies and initiatives to improve diets and prevent chronic diseases.
paras.zh: 然而，这些研究并没有解释为什么会这样，而这个问题对于制定有效的政策和举措以改善饮食、预防慢性病有着重大意义。

paras.en: Public-health initiatives to promote healthy diets often focus on providing nutrition education and recipes (食谱).
paras.zh: 旨在促进健康饮食的公共卫生举措往往侧重于提供营养教育和食谱。

paras.en: These approaches, however, often presume less food literacy (i.e. food knowledge and skills) among low-income people.
paras.zh: 然而，这些做法往往预先假定低收入人群的食物素养（即有关食物的知识和技能）较低。

paras.en: Are unhealthy diets really the result of poor choices, limited food skills and knowledge?
paras.zh: 不健康的饮食真的是选择不当、食物技能和知识有限的结果吗？

paras.en: Research suggests that adults in food-insecure households are just as likely as those in food-secure households to adjust recipes to make them more healthy.
paras.zh: 研究表明，食物无保障家庭中的成年人调整食谱、使其更健康的可能性，和食物有保障家庭中的成年人一样大。

paras.en: They are also just as proficient in food preparation and cooking skills.
paras.zh: 他们在食物准备和烹饪技能方面也同样熟练。

paras.en: There is no indication that increasing food skills or budgeting skills will reduce food insecurity.
paras.zh: 没有迹象表明，提高食物技能或预算规划技能会减轻食物无保障的状况。

paras.en: Instead, disadvantaged groups are constrained by their economic, material and social circumstances.
paras.zh: 相反，弱势群体受制于自身的经济、物质和社会状况。

paras.en: For example, low income is the strongest predictor of food insecurity in Canada, where one in eight households experiences insufficient access to nutritious foods.
paras.zh: 例如，在加拿大，低收入是食物无保障最有力的预测因素；在那里，每八户家庭中就有一户无法充分获得有营养的食物。

w.m: n. 预测因素；预测指标

paras.en: It’s well-established that food prices are an important determinant of food choice.
paras.zh: 食物价格是食物选择的一个重要决定因素，这一点早有定论。

w.m: adj. 已被充分证实的；公认的

paras.en: Low-income households report that they find it difficult to adopt dietary guidelines because food prices are a barrier to improving their diets.
paras.zh: 低收入家庭表示，他们觉得很难采纳膳食指南，因为食物价格是他们改善饮食的障碍。

paras.en: When researchers estimate the cost of diets people actually eat, higher-quality diets are typically more costly.
paras.zh: 从研究人员对人们实际饮食成本的估算来看，质量较高的饮食通常更贵。

paras.en: While this may be so, it does not, in itself, prove that healthy diets are necessarily more expensive or cost-prohibitive.
paras.zh: 虽然情况或许如此，但这本身并不能证明健康饮食必然更贵，或贵得令人望而却步。

w.m: adj. 价格高得令人望而却步的

paras.en: After all, not all socioeconomically disadvantaged people consume poor diets.
paras.zh: 毕竟，并非所有社会经济地位处于弱势的人都吃得很差。

paras.en: We can easily think of a number of foods and recipes that are both inexpensive and nutritious.
paras.zh: 我们很容易就能想到不少既便宜又有营养的食物和食谱。

paras.en: The internet is full of recipes for “eating well on a budget.”
paras.zh: 网上到处都是“花小钱吃得好”的食谱。

passages.name: 2023年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 追求大房子的代价
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与伦理
passages.summary: 美国正面临住房危机，流行文化和住房行业却把幸福推销成拥有更大的空间和更多的便利设施；这一点也体现在住宅上：1970年以前建造的独栋住宅平均面积不到1,500平方英尺，而到2016年，新建独栋住宅的平均面积为2,422平方英尺。作者指出，住大房子会带来后果：大房子打理起来费时间，需要清洁工等低薪服务人员来维护；曾经的公共空间日益私有化，人人可用的公共设施随之减少，许多人的生活质量也下降了。作者认为，中产阶级和上层阶级靠他人的低薪劳动过奢华生活、富人购买的便利设施增多意味着穷人的便利设施减少，这两种制度都不可接受；比起为一部分人建造更大的房子，更好的目标是为所有人创造更多向公众开放的空间和便利设施。

paras.en: The United States is facing a housing crisis: Affordable housing is inadequate, while luxury homes abound (充裕), and homelessness remains a persistent problem.
paras.zh: 美国正面临一场住房危机：平价住房供应不足，豪宅却比比皆是，无家可归也依然是一个长期存在的问题。

w.m: 平价住房（中低收入者负担得起的住房）
v. 大量存在；比比皆是
adj. 长期存在的；顽固的

paras.en: Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities (便利设施).
paras.zh: 尽管如此，流行文化和住房行业却把幸福推销成这样一种生活：既有更大的空间，又有更多的便利设施。

paras.en: Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury.
paras.zh: 大房子被宣传成辛勤工作与勤奋努力的回报，住房也因此从一种基本必需品变成了奢侈品。

paras.en: This is reflected in our homes.
paras.zh: 这一点体现在我们的住宅上。

w.m: 体现在……上；在……中得到反映

paras.en: The average single-family home built in the United States before 1970 was less than 1,500 square feet in size.
paras.zh: 1970年以前在美国建造的独栋住宅，平均面积不到1,500平方英尺。

w.m: 独栋住宅（供一户人家居住）

paras.en: By 2016, the average size of a new single-family home was 2,422 square feet.
paras.zh: 到2016年，新建独栋住宅的平均面积为2,422平方英尺。

w.m: 独栋住宅（供一户人家居住）

paras.en: What’s more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages.
paras.zh: 此外，与早期的房型相比，21世纪头十年建造的住宅更有可能各类空间都更多：卧室、浴室、客厅、餐厅、娱乐室和车库。

paras.en: There are consequences of living big.
paras.zh: 住大房子是有后果的。

paras.en: As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened.
paras.zh: 随着中产阶级的住房越变越大，出现了两种情况。

paras.en: First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order.
paras.zh: 首先，大房子打理起来费时间，所以需要清洁工和其他低薪服务人员来让这些房子保持整洁有序。

paras.en: Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many.
paras.zh: 其次，曾经的公共空间是来自不同背景的人们过去常常相聚的地方，如今却越来越多地被私有化了，导致人人可用的公共设施数量减少，许多人的生活质量也随之下降。

w.m: adj. 降低了的；减少了的

paras.en: Take swimming pools.
paras.zh: 以游泳池为例。

paras.en: While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million.
paras.zh: 1950年，美国只有2,500个家庭拥有游泳池，而到了1999年，这一数字达到了400万。

paras.en: At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim.
paras.zh: 与此同时，市政公共游泳池往往遭到关闭，让低收入人群无处游泳。

paras.en: The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions.
paras.zh: 因此，追求更大住房的趋势引发了伦理问题。

paras.en: Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others?
paras.zh: 中产阶级和上层阶级利用他人的低薪劳动，享受着奢华的生活方式，美国人应该接受这样一种制度吗？

paras.en: Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor?
paras.zh: 富人购买的便利设施增多，就意味着穷人能享有的便利设施减少，我们愿意接受这样一种制度吗？

paras.en: I believe neither is acceptable.
paras.zh: 我认为两者都不可接受。

paras.en: We must change the way we think: living well does not need to mean having more private spaces; instead, it could mean having more public spaces.
paras.zh: 我们必须改变思维方式：过得好不必意味着拥有更多私人空间，而是可以意味着拥有更多公共空间。

paras.en: A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all.
paras.zh: 比起为一部分人建造更大的房子，更好的目标是为所有人创造更多向公众开放的空间和便利设施。

w.m: 向公众开放的；公众可使用的

passages.name: 2023年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 过度的雄心可能弊大于利
passages.genre: 议论文 · 创业与人生
passages.summary: 创业圈里的大多数人雄心高于平均水平，这总体上是一种积极的品质，但在某些情况下，过度的雄心最终可能弊大于利：它容易让人过于执着于某个特定的愿景，从而难以适应新情况；而在最有雄心的创业者看来，失败是灾难性的、不可能从中恢复的。雄心勃勃的人在物质上往往更成功，却只比雄心较小的人稍微快乐一点，寿命也往往明显更短。作者认为，一定程度的雄心对人的积极性有好处，但雄心过度也可能让人面临倦怠、固执乃至寿命缩短的风险。

paras.en: Most of us in the entrepreneurial community are blessed—or cursed—with higher-than-average ambition.
paras.zh: 我们创业圈里的大多数人都有幸——或者说不幸——拥有高于平均水平的雄心。

w.m: v. 使受困扰（be cursed with 不幸有着）

paras.en: Ambitious people strongly desire accomplishments and are willing to take more risks and spend more effort to get them.
paras.zh: 雄心勃勃的人强烈渴望取得成就，也愿意为此承担更多风险、付出更多努力。

w.m: adj. 有雄心的；雄心勃勃的

paras.en: Overall, this is a positive quality, especially for people trying to build their own businesses.
paras.zh: 总体而言，这是一种积极的品质，对那些努力创办自己企业的人来说尤其如此。

paras.en: Apparently, if you’re more naturally driven to set goals, you are more likely to succeed.
paras.zh: 看起来，如果你天生更有动力去设定目标，你就更有可能成功。

w.m: adj. 有动力的；受驱使的

paras.en: Actually, this isn’t always the case.
paras.zh: 实际上，情况并非总是如此。

paras.en: In fact, in some cases, extreme ambition may end up doing more harm than good.
paras.zh: 事实上，在某些情况下，极度的雄心最终可能弊大于利。

paras.en: One major side effect of excessive ambition is the tendency to focus too determinedly on one particular vision or end goal.
paras.zh: 过度的雄心有一个主要的副作用，就是容易让人过于执意地专注于某一个特定的愿景或最终目标。

paras.en: This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur.
paras.zh: 这之所以成问题，是因为它会妨碍你适应新情况的能力，而如果你想成为一名成功的创业者，这种能力至关重要。

w.m: adj. 有问题的；成问题的

paras.en: If a new competitor emerges to threaten your business, you may need to change direction, even if that means straying from your original vision.
paras.zh: 如果有新的竞争对手出现，威胁到你的企业，你可能就需要改变方向，即使这意味着偏离你最初的愿景。

paras.en: If you have too much ambition, you’ll find this hard, if not impossible.
paras.zh: 如果你的雄心太大，你会发现这即使并非不可能，也很难做到。

paras.en: Few people are successful when they try to build their first brand.
paras.zh: 很少有人在尝试打造自己的第一个品牌时就取得成功。

w.m: adj. 很少的；几乎没有的

paras.en: Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and impossible to recover from.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，在最有雄心的创业者看来，失败是灾难性的，不可能从中恢复过来。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: It’s a clear departure from the intended plan toward the intended goal.
paras.zh: 失败明显偏离了通向既定目标的既定计划。

paras.en: For people with limited ambition, however, failure is viewed as something closer to reality.
paras.zh: 然而，在雄心有限的人看来，失败是一件更贴近现实的事。

paras.en: Remember, failure is inevitable, and every failure you survive is a learning experience.
paras.zh: 记住，失败是不可避免的，而你挺过的每一次失败，都是一次学习的经历。

w.m: 学习经历；长见识的经历

paras.en: Ambitious people tend to be more materially successful than their non-ambitious counterparts.
paras.zh: 与没有雄心的人相比，雄心勃勃的人在物质上往往更成功。

w.m: adj. 有雄心的；雄心勃勃的

paras.en: However, they’re only slightly happier than their less-ambitious counterparts, and tend to live significantly shorter lives.
paras.zh: 然而，他们只比雄心较小的人稍微快乐一点，而且寿命往往明显更短。

w.m: 过……的一生（live shorter lives 寿命更短）

paras.en: This implies that even though ambitious people are more likely to achieve conventional “success,” such success means nothing for their health and happiness—and if you don’t have health and happiness, what else could possibly matter?
paras.zh: 这表明，尽管雄心勃勃的人更有可能取得传统意义上的“成功”，但这种成功对他们的健康和幸福毫无意义——而如果你没有健康和幸福，其他的又怎么可能重要呢？

w.m: adj. 有雄心的；雄心勃勃的
adv. （用于疑问句，加强语气）可能；究竟

paras.en: Clearly, some amount of ambition is good for your motivation.
paras.zh: 显然，一定程度的雄心对你的积极性有好处。

paras.en: Without any ambition, you wouldn’t start your own business, set or achieve goals, or get far in life.
paras.zh: 如果没有一点雄心，你就不会创办自己的企业，不会设定或实现目标，在人生道路上也走不远。

w.m: 创办自己的企业；自己创业

paras.en: But an excess of ambition can also be dangerous, putting you at risk of burnout, stubbornness and even a shorter life.
paras.zh: 但雄心过度也可能很危险，会让你面临倦怠、固执甚至寿命缩短的风险。

passages.name: 2023年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 员工为何反感团队建设活动
passages.genre: 说明文 · 职场与管理
passages.summary: 悉尼大学研究人员发表论文，报告了参与者对团队建设干预措施的感受，揭示出强迫员工参与所涉及的伦理问题。研究发现，侧重于分享和干预个人态度及成员之间关系的团队建设活动被认为过于强硬，也过于干涉私事；许多人不想被迫去玩乐或交朋友。研究人员推荐一种自我表露的方法，但指出它要想成功就必须出于自愿；马图斯博士还认为，许多用于改善团队和组织的关系类方法可以谨慎地从其他领域借鉴过来，问题在于如何有效运用这些方法来加强整个集体。

paras.en: Team-building exercises have become popular for managers trying to increase organisational and team harmony and productivity.
paras.zh: 对于力图提升组织和团队的和谐度与生产率的管理者来说，团队建设活动已经变得很受欢迎。

w.m: n. （有特定目的的）活动；训练

paras.en: Unfortunately many employees resent compulsory bonding and often regard these exercises as a nuisance.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，许多员工反感被迫去增进彼此的感情，还常常把这些活动视为麻烦事。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是
n. 增进感情；建立情感纽带
n. （有特定目的的）活动；训练

paras.en: A paper published this week by University of Sydney researchers in Social Networks has reported participants’ feelings about team-building interventions (干预), revealing ethical implications in forcing employees to take part.
paras.zh: 悉尼大学的研究人员本周在《社会网络》期刊上发表了一篇论文，报告了参与者对团队建设干预措施的感受，揭示出强迫员工参与所涉及的伦理问题。

w.m: n. 涉及的问题；（可能的）影响

paras.en: “Many people see team-building activities as a waste of time, so we decided to look in more depth at what’s behind this,” said the paper’s lead researcher, Dr Peter Matous.
paras.zh: “许多人把团队建设活动看作浪费时间，所以我们决定更深入地探究这背后的原因，”论文的首席研究员彼得·马图斯博士说。

paras.en: “Teams are formed, combined and restructured.
paras.zh: “团队经历组建、合并与重组。

paras.en: Staff are relocated and office spaces redesigned.
paras.zh: 员工调换办公地点，办公空间重新设计。

w.m: n. 员工（总称）；全体职员
v. 调换（工作）地点；迁移

paras.en: All this is done with the aim of improving workplace efficiency, collaboration and cohesion.
paras.zh: 所有这一切，都是为了提升工作场所的效率、协作水平和凝聚力。

paras.en: But does any of this work?” said Dr Matous.
paras.zh: 但这些做法中有任何一项奏效吗？”马图斯博士说。

paras.en: The study found that team-building exercises which focused on the sharing of and intervening in personal attitudes and relationships between team members were considered too heavy-handed and intrusive, although the researchers say some degree of openness and vulnerability is often necessary to make deep, effective connections with colleagues.
paras.zh: 研究发现，有些团队建设活动侧重于分享和干预团队成员的个人态度以及成员之间的关系，这类活动被认为过于强硬，也过于干涉私事；不过研究人员表示，要与同事建立深入而有效的联系，往往需要在一定程度上敞开心扉、展露自己的脆弱。

w.m: n. （有特定目的的）活动；训练
adj. 干涉（他人私事）的；侵扰的
一定程度的；在一定程度上
n. 脆弱；（展露）脆弱的一面

paras.en: “Some participants were against team-building exercises because they were implicitly compulsory.
paras.zh: “一些参与者反对团队建设活动，因为这些活动是变相强制的。

w.m: n. （有特定目的的）活动；训练

paras.en: They didn’t welcome management’s interest in their lives beyond their direct work performance,” said Matous.
paras.zh: 他们不欢迎管理层关注自己直接工作表现以外的生活，”马图斯说。

paras.en: “Many people don’t want to be forced into having fun or making friends, especially not on top of their busy jobs.
paras.zh: “许多人不想被迫去玩乐或交朋友，尤其不想在本已繁忙的工作之外还要这样做。

paras.en: They feel management is being too nosy or trying to control their lives too much.”
paras.zh: 他们觉得管理层太爱打听，或是试图过多地控制他们的生活。”

w.m: adj. 爱打听的；好管闲事的

paras.en: In this study the researchers recommended a self-disclosure (表露) approach where participants were guided through a series of questions that allowed them to increasingly disclose personal information and values.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员推荐了一种自我表露的方法：在引导下，参与者依次回答一系列问题，这些问题让他们能够越来越多地透露个人信息和价值观。

w.m: 引导（某人）逐一完成；带领……经历

paras.en: The method is well-tested and has been shown to increase interpersonal closeness.
paras.zh: 这种方法经过了充分检验，已被证明能增进人际亲密感。

paras.en: However, to be successful it must be voluntary.
paras.zh: 不过，这种方法要想成功，就必须出于自愿。

paras.en: The researchers said there are numerous schools of thought that propose differing psychological methods for strengthening relationships.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，有众多学派提出各不相同的心理学方法来加强人际关系。

paras.en: “With caution, many relational methods to improve teams and organisations can be borrowed from other fields.
paras.zh: “许多用于改善团队和组织的关系类方法，都可以谨慎地从其他领域借鉴过来。

w.m: adj. 关系的；与（人际）关系有关的

paras.en: The question is how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective, which is more than just the sum of individual relationships,” said Dr Matous.
paras.zh: 问题在于如何有效地运用这些方法来加强整个集体，而集体不仅仅是各个单独关系的总和，”马图斯博士说。

passages.name: 2023年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 洛杉矶县的无家可归问题
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与民生
passages.summary: 洛杉矶县有近58,000名无家可归者。该县公民在2016年11月和2017年3月两次投票，决定给自己加税，为一项面向无家可归者、为期10年、耗资数十亿美元的住房和社会服务计划提供资金，洛杉矶由此迎来了几十年来应对无家可归问题的最好机会，作者认为这个机会绝不能浪费。作者指出，与普遍看法相反，洛杉矶的无家可归者大多并没有精神疾病，也不吸毒成瘾，越来越大比例的人流落街头是因为运气不好、一连串失误或被经济遗忘，而该县无家可归人口的增长速度超过了新住房的供应速度。在世界上最富有的国家，如此规模的无家可归现象理应令人羞愧和震惊，但大多数洛杉矶居民已不再感到震惊或羞愧，同情心正在被听天由命的心态取代。

paras.en: There are close to 58,000 homeless people in Los Angeles County.
paras.zh: 洛杉矶县有近58,000名无家可归者。

paras.en: That’s a shocking and tragic number for a region that’s home to some of the richest people in the world.
paras.zh: 对于一个住着世界上一些最富有之人的地区来说，这个数字令人震惊，也令人痛心。

w.m: adj. 悲惨的；令人痛心的
