paras.zh: 对于《卫报》所称的这一“最佳点”，他们得出的结论与所谓的“金发姑娘原则”相符，即某样东西的量可以恰到好处。

w.m: 金发姑娘原则（凡事恰到好处为宜）

paras.en: The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.
paras.zh: 这一概念已应用于广泛的学科领域，从发展心理学到经济学，再到工程学。

paras.en: Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.
paras.zh: 牛津大学保护生物学教授克劳迪奥·西列罗对该报表示，这些新发现的意义可能不止于大熊猫保护。

paras.en: “Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes,” said Sillero, who was not involved in the research.
paras.zh: “大多数大型食肉动物都生活在日益破碎化的景观中，”并未参与这项研究的西列罗说。

w.m: adj. 破碎化的；支离破碎的

paras.en: “It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human endeavour induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence.”
paras.zh: “很可能，它们与人类活动之间关系的混乱性质促使更多动物分散开来或走得更远，并可能带来更强的遗传连通性，增强种群的存续能力。”

paras.en: The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.
paras.zh: 最近一次大熊猫数量统计发现，野外现存1800多只大熊猫，它们因此被列入易危物种名单，而非濒危物种名单。

passages.name: 2025年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 坚毅：通往成功的新钥匙
passages.genre: 议论文 · 成功与个人成长
passages.summary: 安杰拉·达克沃思在《坚毅》一书中提出，天赋可能被高估了，想要真正的成功，需要的是坚毅，即激情与坚持的完美结合。文章认为，坚毅告诉我们完美并不是目标，它卸下了压在我们肩上的不合理期望，让我们得以重新定义目标。即使还没有掌握某项技能，如果能把激情转化为行动，仍然可以成功；如果一开始失败了，就凭着坚毅再试一次。

paras.en: With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying.
paras.zh: 对于那些生来就有天赋的人，感觉他们好像不怎么费力就能出类拔萃。

w.m: adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: But what about those of us who don’t have a natural talent?
paras.zh: 可是，我们当中那些没有天赋的人又当如何呢？

w.m: adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: We’ve been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed.
paras.zh: 我们一辈子都听人说：如果你努力，你也能成功。

paras.en: But with the release of Angela Duckworth’s Grit, we are given a new key to success.
paras.zh: 但随着安杰拉·达克沃思的《坚毅》一书出版，我们得到了一把通往成功的新钥匙。

w.m: n. 坚毅；坚韧不拔（此处为书名《坚毅》）

paras.en: “As much as talent counts, effort counts twice,” says Duckworth in Grit.
paras.zh: “天赋固然重要，但努力的分量是它的两倍，”达克沃思在《坚毅》中说。

w.m: 尽管；虽然（引导让步从句）
n. 坚毅；坚韧不拔（此处为书名《坚毅》）

paras.en: She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence.
paras.zh: 她提出了一个新观念：天赋可能被高估了；如果你想获得真正的成功，你需要的是坚毅，即激情与坚持的完美结合。

paras.en: Even if you have natural talent, it’s nothing without grit.
paras.zh: 即使你有天赋，没有坚毅，天赋也算不了什么。

w.m: adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure.
paras.zh: 达克沃思说，成功与失败的差别就在于坚毅。

paras.en: A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not.
paras.zh: 有坚毅品质的人比没有这种品质的人更有可能成功。

paras.en: When we think about attaining success—whether it’s landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn.
paras.zh: 每当我们想到要取得成功——无论是拿下那份工作，还是学会那项新技能——思绪立刻就会被必须先学的一切压得沉甸甸的。

w.m: v. 得到；拿下（工作、合同等）
v. 使负重担；使不堪重负

paras.en: If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then how to dress the part—and you must be perfect at all of them.
paras.zh: 如果你想得到那份新工作，就得学会工作技能，然后是面试技能，再然后是如何穿着得体、符合身份——而且每一项你都必须做到完美。

w.m: 穿着与身份相称；打扮得像样

paras.en: Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn’t the goal.
paras.zh: 坚毅之所以不同，是因为它告诉我们，完美并不是目标。

paras.en: Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders.
paras.zh: 坚毅卸下了压在我们肩上的不合理期望。

paras.en: Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible.
paras.zh: 坚毅告诉我们，那扇门敞开得比我们起初想象的还要宽。

paras.en: Grit allows us to redefine our goals.
paras.zh: 坚毅让我们得以重新定义自己的目标。

paras.en: Think about it: what’s something you’ve always wanted to do, but gave up because you “don’t have the skills for it”?
paras.zh: 想一想：有什么事是你一直想做，却因为你“不具备做这件事的技能”而放弃了的？

paras.en: What’s something you love but aren’t good at?
paras.zh: 又有什么事是你热爱、却并不擅长的？

paras.en: The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try.
paras.zh: 坚毅真正的运作方式，是拥有持久的激情，并不断尝试。

w.m: n. 运作方式；工作原理
adj. 可持续的；能持久的

paras.en: Effort means more than your natural ability.
paras.zh: 努力比你天生的能力更重要。

w.m: v. 有重要性；有意义（mean more than 意为“比……更重要”）
adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: Even if you haven’t mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action.
paras.zh: 即使你还没有掌握某项技能，坚毅也告诉你：如果你能把激情转化为行动，你仍然可以成功。

paras.en: In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams.
paras.zh: 从某种意义上说，达克沃思正在给那些已经对自己的梦想关上大门的人带来新的希望。

w.m: 从某种意义上说；在某种程度上
对……关上大门；断绝……的念头

paras.en: She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything.
paras.zh: 她是在说，你做成任何事都是有可能的。

paras.en: If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit.
paras.zh: 如果一开始失败了，那就凭着坚毅再试一次。

passages.name: 2025年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 衣着如何影响心态与行为
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与生活
passages.summary: 我们都会为特殊场合花心思打扮，但大多数人对精心打扮怀有矛盾的心理。科学研究表明，由于我们赋予不同服装象征意义，所穿的衣服会影响我们的行为、情绪乃至与他人互动的方式。彰显权势的服装让人更自信，进而有助于我们成为更出色的谈判者和抽象思考者；但穿正装时人们往往没那么开放、没那么容易放松，便装则有助于我们变得更友善、更有创造力，这些发现支持了周五穿商务休闲装这一想法。

paras.en: We all make a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions.
paras.zh: 我们都会为特殊场合多下一点功夫，让自己看起来体面一些。

paras.en: But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes.
paras.zh: 但我们大多数人对精心打扮怀有矛盾的心理，也会因为花时间关注衣着而感到内疚。

w.m: adj. 相互矛盾的；冲突的

paras.en: Science now suggests the right dress may give us the extra edge in our professional and personal lives.
paras.zh: 如今科学表明，合适的着装或许能让我们在职业和个人生活中多一分优势。

paras.en: We hear sayings like “dress for the job you want, not the job you have”.
paras.zh: 我们会听到“为你想要的工作着装，而不是为你现有的工作着装”之类的说法。

paras.en: Most people don’t really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings.
paras.zh: 大多数人并不真的相信这些说法，但如今对衣着如何影响行为的研究表明，这些说法或许确实有一点道理。

paras.en: Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing.
paras.zh: 科学告诉我们，由于我们给不同类型的服装赋予了象征意义，所穿的衣服会影响我们的行为和情绪，甚至影响我们与他人互动的方式。

paras.en: We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on.
paras.zh: 我们认为有些衣服很有气势，有些衣服很有趣，诸如此类。

w.m: adj. 有气势的；强有力的

paras.en: We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes.
paras.zh: 我们甚至会根据衣着来评价刚认识的人。

paras.en: We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way it makes us feel.
paras.zh: 我们也会根据自己身上穿的衣服来评价自己，原因就在于这身衣服带给我们的感觉。

paras.en: This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior.
paras.zh: 这意味着，穿某件衣服的体验会影响我们的态度和行为选择。

paras.en: There’s a reason tailored jackets are associated with being “dressed for success”.
paras.zh: 人们把剪裁合身的西装外套和“为成功而着装”联系在一起，是有原因的。

w.m: adj. 剪裁合身的；量身定做的

paras.en: It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business.
paras.zh: 看来，穿上正式的职业装能让我们进入适合处理业务的心态。

paras.en: Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance.
paras.zh: 穿上彰显权势的服装会让我们感觉更自信，甚至会增加展现支配地位所需的激素。

w.m: 彰显权势的服装；权力着装
n. 支配地位；主导地位

paras.en: This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers.
paras.zh: 这进而帮助我们成为更出色的谈判者和抽象思考者。

paras.en: While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn’t a great idea when we want to socialize.
paras.zh: 虽然在董事会会议室里，一套好西装对我们的表现有奇效，但想要社交时，穿正装就不是什么好主意了。

paras.en: Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes.
paras.zh: 研究发现，人们穿正装时往往没那么开放，也没那么容易放松。

paras.en: On the other hand, casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative.
paras.zh: 另一方面，便装有助于我们变得更友善、更有创造力。

paras.en: These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday, since colleagues are most likely to take time out to socialize on the last work day of the week.
paras.zh: 这些发现支持了周五穿商务休闲装这一想法，因为在一周的最后一个工作日，同事们最有可能抽出时间来社交。

paras.en: I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?
paras.zh: 我的意思是，谁会想和穿着西装的人一起消磨时光呢？

w.m: 和……一起消磨时光；和……一起玩

passages.name: 2025年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 歌剧与古典音乐仍有现实意义
passages.genre: 议论文 · 音乐与文化
passages.summary: 随着流行音乐、爵士乐和电子音乐的兴起，歌剧和古典音乐开始淡出公众视野，但作者认为它们如今依然颇具活力。当下许多流行音乐所用的节拍、和声与旋律都与一些古典音乐杰作相似；摇滚歌剧的发明、古典乐曲在现代电影中用作背景音乐、专为大制作电影创作的交响管弦乐作品，也都体现了它们的现实意义。作者认为，古典音乐和歌剧是现代音乐的基础，鉴于它们对当今社会的巨大影响，可以预期它们在未来几个世纪里仍会保持重要地位。

paras.en: With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye.
paras.zh: 随着流行音乐、爵士乐和电子音乐的兴起，歌剧和古典音乐都开始淡出公众视野。

paras.en: Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music.
paras.zh: 一些人开始怀疑，歌剧和古典音乐对现代音乐世界是否仍有现实意义。

paras.en: Granted, you will not typically see today’s teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.
paras.zh: 诚然，短期内你一般不会看到如今的青少年去聆听巴赫，但有一些重要迹象表明，歌剧和古典音乐如今都依然颇具活力。

paras.en: The most significant indicator of classical music’s importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies (旋律) to those that were used in some of classical music’s best works.
paras.zh: 古典音乐在当今社会中的重要性，其最显著的迹象就是这样一个事实：当下正在制作的很多流行音乐，所用的节拍、和声与旋律都与古典音乐中某些最优秀作品所用的相似。

paras.en: Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic (交响乐的) orchestras have had on society’s taste in music.
paras.zh: 即便如此，不学乐理的人可能很难把这一点看作一种迹象，因为它不易察觉，只是体现出交响乐团对社会的音乐品味所产生的影响。

w.m: adj. 不易察觉的；微妙的

paras.en: A better example of the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera.
paras.zh: 更能说明歌剧和古典音乐现实意义的一个例子，可以从摇滚歌剧的发明中看到。

paras.en: Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form.
paras.zh: 按最简单的定义来说，歌剧就是以音乐为形式来讲述故事。

paras.en: The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least.
paras.zh: 用音乐讲述故事这门艺术丝毫没有衰落。

paras.en: In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself.
paras.zh: 事实上，歌剧本身的主要部分有时会用到真正的管弦乐团。

paras.en: Some of the world’s greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.
paras.zh: 世界上一些最热门的歌曲曾是摇滚歌剧的组成部分。

w.m: n. 热门歌曲；风靡一时的事物

paras.en: Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive.
paras.zh: 古典音乐的爱好者也能告诉你，比古典音乐更富表现力的音乐类型寥寥无几。

w.m: det. 很少的；几乎没有的

paras.en: So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies.
paras.zh: 所以，古典乐曲仍在现代电影中用作背景音乐，这应该不会让任何人感到意外。

paras.en: Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures.
paras.zh: 还有一些交响管弦乐作品，纯粹是为了用在大制作电影中而创作的。

paras.en: These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.
paras.zh: 这些作品在主流音乐爱好者中往往很受欢迎。

paras.en: Classical music and opera are the very foundation upon which our modern music is based.
paras.zh: 古典音乐和歌剧正是我们现代音乐赖以建立的基础。

paras.en: Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, there is no doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.
paras.zh: 考虑到它们对我们当今社会产生的巨大影响，毫无疑问，我们可以预期它们在未来几个世纪里会继续保持重要地位。

passages.name: 2025年6月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 美貌之外：培养内在美
passages.genre: 议论文 · 生活与情感
passages.summary: 我们的社会十分看重外貌之美。作者认为，努力让自己显得好看并没有错，但过分关注外表会忽略美在心灵层面的内涵，还可能让我们始终没有培养起维系并加深亲密关系所必需的内在品质；正是做真实自我的勇气，让我们在更深的层面上彼此联结。培养内在美的道路很简单，却未必容易：并非每个人都会欣赏真实的我们，但我们最终会找到那些心灵契合、欣赏我们本来样子的人。

paras.en: Our society places a high value on physical beauty.
paras.zh: 我们的社会非常看重外貌之美。

paras.en: Americans spend an average of over $722 each year on their appearance.
paras.zh: 美国人每年在外表上的花费平均超过722美元。

paras.en: One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star.
paras.zh: 每十个美国人中就有一个曾试图让自己看起来像明星。

w.m: 每十个中就有一个；十分之一

paras.en: There’s nothing wrong with trying to look our best, but excessive focus on physical appearance misses the soulful aspects of what it means to be beautiful.
paras.zh: 努力让自己显得最好看并没有什么错，但过分关注外表，就会忽略美丽的内涵中那些关乎心灵的方面。

w.m: 显得最好看；处于最佳状态
adj. 关乎心灵的；深情的

paras.en: Trying to look like the magazine pictures can take us on a long ride away from what beauty is really about.
paras.zh: 努力让自己看起来像杂志照片上那样，可能会让我们在偏离美之真谛的路上越走越远。

paras.en: Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection.
paras.zh: 我们当中许多人花了实在太多的时间、精力和金钱，努力打磨一个我们认为能带来关注、爱和情感联结的形象。

paras.en: In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning.
paras.zh: 在这个过程中，我们可能没能以一种能引领我们走向更深的亲密关系、满足感和意义感的方式来关照自己。

paras.en: It may sound trite (老生常谈的), but beauty is only skin deep; it’s not what brings love toward us.
paras.zh: 这话听起来或许是老生常谈，但美貌只是表面的；为我们带来爱的并不是它。

w.m: adj. 陈腐的；老生常谈的
美貌只是表面的；美丽是肤浅的（谚语）

paras.en: Just read about the latest Hollywood starlets whose seeming love turns into resentment and bitter court battles.
paras.zh: 只要读一读好莱坞最新一批年轻女星的报道就知道了：她们表面上的爱情变成了怨恨和一场场激烈的官司。

w.m: adj. 激烈的；充满怨恨的

paras.en: Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing.
paras.zh: 外在美可能是一种福分，但也同样可能是一种祸根。

w.m: 和……同样是；在同等程度上是

paras.en: We may develop a habit of being so focused on maintaining a perfect appearance that we never cultivate the inner qualities necessary to sustain and deepen intimacy and connection.
paras.zh: 我们可能会养成一种习惯，过于专注于保持完美的外表，以至于从来不去培养维系并加深亲密关系与情感联结所必需的内在品质。

paras.en: As I describe in my book, The Authentic Heart, it is the courage to be authentic that connects us in a deeper way.
paras.zh: 正如我在自己的书《真实之心》中所阐述的，正是做真实自我的勇气，让我们在更深的层面上彼此联结。

paras.en: While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long.
paras.zh: 虽然我们最初被对方吸引，可能在一定程度上是基于身体上的化学反应，但正是彼此内心世界的交汇，才会造就我们所渴望的持久亲密关系与心灵联结。

w.m: n. （人与人之间的）化学反应；来电

paras.en: If we redirect our attention toward cultivating inner qualities, we might find a magnetic attraction that moves us from something superficial to something that connects us to our depths.
paras.zh: 如果我们把注意力转向培养内在品质，或许会发现一种磁石般的吸引力，它让我们从流于表面的东西，转向能将我们与内心深处相联结的东西。

w.m: adj. 有磁力的；有吸引力的

paras.en: The path toward cultivating inner beauty is really simple.
paras.zh: 培养内在美的道路真的很简单。

paras.en: But what is simple is not always easy.
paras.zh: 但简单的事并不总是容易做到。

w.m: 并不总是；未必（部分否定）

paras.en: Not everyone will see us and appreciate us as we take the courageous risk to allow ourselves to be seen as we really are.
paras.zh: 当我们鼓起勇气冒险，允许自己以真实的样子被人看见时，并不是每个人都会看见我们、欣赏我们。

paras.en: But if they don’t, it is their loss, not ours.
paras.zh: 但如果他们做不到，那是他们的损失，不是我们的。

w.m: 那是某人的损失；那是某人自己吃亏

paras.en: Eventually we’ll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.
paras.zh: 最终，我们会找到那些与我们心灵契合、欣赏我们本来样子的人。

passages.name: 2025年6月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 植物肉的兴起与健康利弊
passages.genre: 说明文 · 饮食与健康
passages.summary: 新一代植物肉在外观、风味和口感上模仿真肉，一份报告预测，到2030年其市场规模将飙升至740亿美元；相关公司瞄准的是爱吃肉但想少吃肉的消费者，而许多素食者其实并不喜欢类似肉的食物。植物肉不含胆固醇，富含多种营养，通常比牛肉更健康，但大多经过高度加工，含钠量高。作者提醒读者别忘了全谷物和蔬菜，并指出豆类营养丰富、价格低廉，比任何加工过的无肉替代品都可持续得多。

paras.en: Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate?
paras.zh: 植物肉很快就会出现在你身边的餐桌上，但它们配得上在你的盘子里占有一席之地吗？

w.m: adj. 以植物为原料的；植物性的

paras.en: If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it’s a good time to give meatless meat another chance.
paras.zh: 如果你多年前尝过蔬菜汉堡，认定它像橡胶一样难嚼、淡而无味而不屑一顾，那么现在正是再给素肉一次机会的好时机。

w.m: 认为……（不值一提）而不予理会
adj. 像橡胶的；（食物）难嚼的

paras.en: Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat.
paras.zh: 较新的品种模仿肉的外观、风味和口感。

paras.en: Analysts don’t expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.
paras.zh: 分析人士预计，无肉运动短期内不会放缓；2021年的一份报告预测，到2030年，这一市场的规模将飙升至740亿美元，增幅达957%。

paras.en: Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians.
paras.zh: 植物肉不再只面向素食者。

w.m: adj. 以植物为原料的；植物性的

paras.en: Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat—the current superstars of the alternative protein sector—are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons.
paras.zh: 像Impossible Foods和Beyond Meat这样的公司是当前替代蛋白领域的超级明星，它们正在争取这样一批消费者：喜欢吃肉，但出于动物权益、健康或环保方面的原因，想减少肉类消费。

paras.en: So far, it’s a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，这一策略很成功：购买Beyond Burger和Impossible Foods产品的消费者中，超过九成也吃肉。

paras.en: Many vegetarians don’t actually care for food that resembles meat.
paras.zh: 许多素食者其实并不喜欢类似肉的食物。

w.m: 喜欢（多用于否定句和疑问句）

paras.en: When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn’t finish it.
paras.zh: 记者琼·索尔斯曼多年来一直是素食者，她尝了一道Impossible Foods的菜，结果恶心得没能吃完。

paras.en: “Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn’t stand to take another bite,” she wrote.
paras.zh: “Impossible Foods已经破解了做出逼真假肉的密码，最能说明这一点的，或许就是我连再吃一口都受不了，”她写道。

paras.en: Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they’re a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber.
paras.zh: 素肉通常是比牛肉更健康的选择，因为它们不含胆固醇，而且还是维生素、矿物质、蛋白质和膳食纤维的良好来源。

paras.en: If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health.
paras.zh: 如果素肉能帮你坚持以植物为主的饮食，这本身就能带来更好的健康状况。

w.m: adj. 以植物为主的；植物性的

paras.en: Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.
paras.zh: 红肉不仅已被发现与癌症有关，而且研究表明，放弃吃肉的人血压更低，平均血糖更低，胆固醇水平也更低。

w.m: 不仅……而且（not only 置于句首时句子部分倒装）

paras.en: However, just because it’s plant-based doesn’t mean it’s health food.
paras.zh: 然而，仅仅因为以植物为原料，并不意味着它就是健康食品。

w.m: adj. 以植物为原料的；植物性的

paras.en: Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium (钠) compared to traditional beef.
paras.zh: 大多数仿制肉都经过高度加工，而且与传统牛肉相比，含钠量很高。

paras.en: These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don’t forget about whole grains and vegetables.
paras.zh: 这些新一代替代肉吸引了全部关注，但别忘了全谷物和蔬菜。

w.m: adj. 替代的；可供选择的

paras.en: Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute.
paras.zh: 豆类是一种尤为出色的蛋白质替代品。

paras.en: They’re nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.
paras.zh: 它们营养丰富，价格低廉，而且比当今市场上任何一种经过加工的无肉替代品都要可持续得多。

w.m: adj. 有营养的；营养丰富的
adj. 便宜的；价格低廉的

passages.name: 2025年12月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 服药时间影响药效
passages.genre: 说明文 · 医学与健康
passages.summary: 地球上的生物都受24小时昼夜周期影响，人体机能和体内许多药物靶点也遵循这一节律，因此在特定时间服药可能有助于提高药效、减少副作用。然而医生开药时很少考虑最佳服药时间，大多数药物也未就昼夜周期中的不同效果做过研究。作者认为，需要更多研究来确定不同疾病的最佳给药时间，考虑服药时间可能有助于让治疗更有效。

paras.en: All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle.
paras.zh: 地球上的所有生物都处在24小时的昼夜周期之中。

paras.en: This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day.
paras.zh: 这一周期就是人们夜间休息、白天活动的原因。

paras.en: Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health.
paras.zh: 因此，人体的所有机能也都遵循这一每日节律，而运动、进食等行为的时间安排会对你的健康产生重大影响。

paras.en: For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage.
paras.zh: 例如，夜间进食久而久之会导致体重增加，因为夜间进食会使脂肪储存增多。

w.m: 久而久之；随着时间推移

paras.en: Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too.
paras.zh: 体内的许多药物靶点也遵循24小时周期。

paras.en: This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period.
paras.zh: 这意味着，药物旨在改变的特定蛋白质，在24小时内的不同时段对药物的反应可能各不相同。

paras.en: Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects.
paras.zh: 由于身体对药物的反应可能因服药时间不同而有所差异，按理说，在特定时间服药可能有助于提高药效、减少不良副作用。

paras.en: When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it.
paras.zh: 医生给人开药时，很少考虑最佳服药时间。

paras.en: There are two main reasons for that oversight.
paras.zh: 这一疏忽主要有两个原因。

paras.en: First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day.
paras.zh: 第一，许多医生并不知道，有些药物在一天中的特定时段效果更好。

paras.en: And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle.
paras.zh: 第二，大多数药物都没有针对它们在24小时周期中可能产生的不同效果做过研究。

paras.en: Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.
paras.zh: 因此，大多数药物都是让患者在早上或晚上服用，这主要是为了确保患者遵医嘱用药。

paras.en: Over 30 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day.
paras.zh: 30多年前，研究人员发现，降胆固醇药物辛伐他汀在夜间服用比在白天服用降胆固醇的效果更好。

w.m: n. 辛伐他汀（一种降胆固醇药）

paras.en: This is because the liver enzyme (酶) this drug targets is more active at night.
paras.zh: 这是因为这种药物所针对的肝脏酶在夜间更为活跃。

paras.en: Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm.
paras.zh: 在错误的时间服药甚至可能造成伤害。

paras.en: My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative (镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night.
paras.zh: 我和同事们想知道，咪达唑仑这种全球外科手术中最常用的镇静剂，是否可能会干扰夜间保护心脏的生物钟。

w.m: n. 咪达唑仑（一种镇静药）

paras.en: Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered.
paras.zh: 目前，对于咪达唑仑应在何时给药，还没有任何指导原则。

w.m: n. 咪达唑仑（一种镇静药）

paras.en: More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases.
paras.zh: 需要更多的研究来确定针对不同疾病实施治疗的最佳时间。

paras.en: I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide.
paras.zh: 我相信，把服药时间考虑在内，可能有助于让治疗更有效，帮助全球更多的人。

passages.name: 2025年12月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 越来越多美国人七十多岁仍在工作
passages.genre: 说明文 · 社会与经济
passages.summary: 在美国，七十多岁仍在工作的人所占比例在过去20年里从不到10%升至近15%：有人是因为想继续工作，有人则是因为需要钱。经济学家认为，除了人们更健康长寿之外，实际工资多年增长缓慢、私营部门逐渐放弃传统养老金等经济因素，以及制造业衰落等变化，都是人们推迟退休的原因。各种受教育程度的人中都出现了这一趋势；一位经济学家认为，许多受过大学教育的人继续工作更多是为了社交方面的好处，而体力要求更高的工作者中仍坚持工作的人更可能是出于经济原因。

paras.en: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser (理发师) about retirement plans.
paras.zh: 经济学教授凯瑟琳·亚伯拉罕当时正和她的理发师聊着退休计划。

paras.en: The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to.
paras.zh: 这位经济学家说，她打算继续工作，因为她自己想工作。

paras.en: The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.
paras.zh: 理发师也有同感，但理由不同：她需要钱。

paras.en: Both scenarios (情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s.
paras.zh: 这两种情况都在促使美国工作到七十多岁的人数大幅增加。

paras.en: Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.
paras.zh: 在过去20年里，七十多岁仍在工作的美国人所占比例已从不到10%升至近15%。

paras.en: In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector is among the reasons people delay retirement.
paras.zh: 经济学家表示，除了人们更加健康、寿命长得多之外，多种财务方面考虑的共同作用也是人们推迟退休的原因之一，比如实际工资多年来增长缓慢，以及私营部门逐渐放弃传统养老金。

paras.en: The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also have contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.
paras.zh: 亚伯拉罕研究美国老年人的工作与退休决策，她说，制造业的衰落以及从事劳动密集程度较低职业的人数增加，也促成了这一趋势。

paras.en: “Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you’re doing,” Abraham says.
paras.zh: “哪个因素更重要，取决于到那时为止你在所从事的工作类型上有着怎样的经历，”亚伯拉罕说。

paras.en: The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category.
paras.zh: 这一总体趋势正波及各种受教育程度的美国人，不过比例因类别而异。

paras.en: The share of Americans with bachelor’s degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018.
paras.zh: 2018年，拥有学士学位的美国人中，工作到七十多岁的人所占比例达到近20%。

paras.en: For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.
paras.zh: 在高中及以下学历的人中，七十多岁仍在工作的比例已升至10%左右，而受过一些大学教育的人则居中，约为15%。

paras.en: Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men.
paras.zh: 马丁·尼尔·贝利是一位经济学家，正在主持一项关于退休保障的研究项目。他指出，放弃职业生涯可能会让人产生孤立感和孤独感，男性尤其如此。

paras.en: He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons.
paras.zh: 他认为，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择留在劳动力队伍中，更多是为了社交方面的好处，而不是出于经济原因。

paras.en: They’re also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.
paras.zh: 他们也更有可能从事专业性职业，在这类职业中他们往往更享受自己的工作。

paras.en: Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.
paras.zh: 贝利说，与此同时，工作对体力要求更高的劳动者可能更盼着退休，这说明他们当中仍坚持工作的人更有可能是出于经济原因才这样做。

w.m: adv. 与此同时；另一方面

passages.name: 2025年12月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 借青少年的叛逆心推广健康饮食
passages.genre: 说明文 · 饮食与健康
passages.summary: 垃圾食品已是许多美国人日常饮食中的主要部分；近期研究表明，肥胖率上升要归咎于不良饮食，而非缺乏锻炼。以往针对青少年的健康饮食干预大多着眼于“未来更健康的你”，可能因此收效不佳；一项大规模研究转而利用青少年的叛逆心、对自主的追求和对社会公正的重视，让他们了解食品行业的操纵与欺骗手段。干预后，参与者对健康饮食的态度有所改变，实际选择食物时也更常挑选健康的零食和饮料。

paras.en: Junk food is now a staple of many Americans’ diets.
paras.zh: 如今，垃圾食品已是许多美国人日常饮食中的主要部分。

paras.en: Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise.
paras.zh: 零食公司的广告宣传常常请体育明星出镜，传递这样一个信息：只要多做体育锻炼，我们就能抵消食用其产品带来的任何负面影响。

w.m: n. （有组织的）系列活动；运动

paras.en: But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates.
paras.zh: 但近期的研究表明，肥胖率上升并不能归咎于缺乏锻炼。

paras.en: Bad diets are.
paras.zh: 该怪的是不良饮食。

paras.en: Interventions (干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers.
paras.zh: 帮助减少垃圾食品摄入的干预措施对儿童和青少年尤其重要。

paras.en: Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat.
paras.zh: 预防胜于治疗，因为肥胖非常难以治疗。

paras.en: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，虽然健康教育在幼儿中取得了一些成效，青少年却一直更难打动。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers’ attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising.
paras.zh: 如今，一项大规模研究尝试用一种创新方法来改变青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果令人鼓舞。

w.m: adj. 有希望的；令人鼓舞的

paras.en: The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，以往的干预措施之所以可能没有成功，是因为存在一个重大缺陷：它们着眼于一个未来更健康的你，并以为这对青少年来说就是足够的动力。

paras.en: In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers’ instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice.
paras.zh: 相比之下，新的干预措施巧妙地利用了青少年叛逆和追求自主的天性，以及他们对社会公正的重视。

paras.en: To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry.
paras.zh: 为此，研究人员让学生阅读了一篇关于食品行业的文章。

paras.en: It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy.
paras.zh: 文章揭露了一个秘密，涉及为使垃圾食品更易让人上瘾、并把这类产品标榜为健康食品而采用的操纵性和欺骗性策略。

paras.en: The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm to these vulnerable groups.
paras.zh: 文章还说明了广告宣传如何专门瞄准年纪很小的人和穷人，给这些弱势群体造成伤害。

w.m: n. （有组织的）系列活动；运动
adj. 弱势的；易受伤害的

paras.en: Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to “fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food.”
paras.zh: 随后，参与者阅读了一份虚构的调查，调查对象是一些想要“通过少买、少吃加工食品来反击这些公司”的青少年。

paras.en: After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice.
paras.zh: 干预之后，参与者把健康饮食与自主和社会公正联系在了一起。

paras.en: The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing.
paras.zh: 这些青少年还把健康饮食评为更有吸引力。

paras.en: Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior.
paras.zh: 重要的是，新的干预措施对实际行为也产生了一些令人鼓舞的效果。

w.m: adj. 有希望的；令人鼓舞的

paras.en: A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context.
paras.zh: 一天后，研究人员在一个看似毫不相关的情境中，让学生们从一些零食和饮料中挑选。

paras.en: The teens more often chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda).
paras.zh: 这些青少年更常选择健康的零食和饮料（如水果或水），而不是不健康的选项（如饼干和汽水）。

paras.en: Associating a healthy diet with teenagers’ own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity.
paras.zh: 把健康饮食与青少年自身的价值观联系起来，似乎是预防肥胖的一条有前景的途径。

w.m: adj. 有希望的；有前景的

passages.name: 2025年12月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 婴儿不做梦：儿童梦境如何发展
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科学与育儿
passages.summary: 婴儿有大量快速眼动睡眠，但科学家认为，这种睡眠对婴儿的作用是帮助大脑形成通路和连接、最终学会语言，而不是做梦，因此婴儿也不会做噩梦。普遍的共识是，孩子大约两岁开始做梦。心理学家福克斯的研究表明，孩子的梦随年龄而发展：很小的孩子的梦多是一些快照，5至9岁的孩子开始梦到活动的画面和接连发生的事件。

paras.en: Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM.
paras.zh: 成年人在快速眼动（REM）睡眠期间做梦，而婴儿有大量的快速眼动睡眠。

paras.en: So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.
paras.zh: 因此，认为婴儿会做很多梦，或许也说得过去。

w.m: adj. 合理的；说得过去的

paras.en: But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming.
paras.zh: 但科学家认为，对新生儿和婴儿来说，快速眼动睡眠的作用完全不同，并不是用来做梦。

paras.en: In babies, REM allows the brain to develop pathways and connections and, eventually, learn languages.
paras.zh: 在婴儿身上，快速眼动睡眠让大脑得以形成通路和连接，并最终学会语言。

paras.en: Since your baby doesn’t dream at this stage of brain development, it’s safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either.
paras.zh: 由于你的宝宝在大脑发育的这个阶段不做梦，可以有把握地认为，宝宝也不会做噩梦。

paras.en: Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma (创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.
paras.zh: 噩梦源于遭受创伤、过度活跃的想象力以及日常生活中的正常压力。

paras.en: Are you wondering what babies dream about?
paras.zh: 你是不是想知道宝宝会梦到些什么？

paras.en: Good question, but the answer is nothing!
paras.zh: 问得好，不过答案是：什么也梦不到！

paras.en: So, when do babies start dreaming?
paras.zh: 那么，宝宝从什么时候开始做梦呢？

paras.en: The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two.
paras.zh: 普遍的共识是，他们大约在两岁时开始做梦。

paras.en: Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day.
paras.zh: 心理学家戴维·福克斯研究儿童（从很小的孩子到青少年），以揭开他们梦境的秘密。

paras.en: In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.
paras.zh: 在他的实验室里，他让孩子们入睡，然后每晚把他们叫醒3次，请他们描述自己记得的内容。

paras.en: Foulkes’ findings are unsurprising.
paras.zh: 福克斯的研究结果并不出人意料。

w.m: adj. 不出所料的；不足为奇的

paras.en: Basically, little kids have little dreams.
paras.zh: 总的来说，小孩子做的梦也小。

paras.en: But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age.
paras.zh: 但孩子在梦中究竟看到什么，取决于他们的年龄。

paras.en: As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.
paras.zh: 随着孩子的发育和成长，他们的梦也在发展。

paras.en: Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots (快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults.
paras.zh: 与成年人的梦相比，很小的孩子的梦通常只是一些快照，看起来更像幻灯片放映，而远不像电影。

paras.en: They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating.
paras.zh: 这些梦里大量出现动物和其他熟悉的景象，比如人们吃东西的画面。

w.m: adv. 大量地；在很大程度上
v. 以……为主要内容；包含

paras.en: According to Foulkes, “Children’s dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration.”
paras.zh: 按照福克斯的说法，“孩子们的梦境生活……似乎与他们清醒时的想象和叙述相似。”

paras.en: Kids ages 5–9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action.
paras.zh: 5至9岁的孩子开始梦到活动的画面和正在行动的角色。

paras.en: Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other.
paras.zh: 此时的梦包含多个串在一起、一个接一个发生的事件。

paras.en: Kids also start developing greater ability to remember dreams.
paras.zh: 孩子们也开始具备更强的记梦能力。

paras.en: Still, that’s not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes’ studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.
paras.zh: 不过，情况并非总是如此：在福克斯的研究中，25%的孩子在快速眼动睡眠期间被唤醒时，不记得自己做过梦，这种趋势一直持续到9岁。

paras.en: So, if your baby seems to be in a stressed state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.
paras.zh: 因此，如果你的宝宝睡觉时似乎处于紧张状态，或者醒来时情绪不安，那可能是其他因素在起作用。

passages.name: 2025年12月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 纯素餐厅摘得米其林三星
passages.genre: 说明文 · 饮食与环保
passages.summary: 纽约的麦迪逊公园11号成为首家获得米其林三星的纯素餐厅。去年，餐厅联合老板兼知名主厨丹尼尔·胡姆以食物体系不可持续为由，把肉类撤下菜单，并承认此举有风险。这次获评证明了这一决定是正确的；胡姆认为，奢侈品企业确实可以发挥作用，也负有责任。

paras.en: New York’s Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan (素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars.
paras.zh: 纽约的麦迪逊公园11号成为首家荣获米其林三星的纯素餐厅。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；素食主义的

paras.en: The fine dining establishment received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes.
paras.zh: 这家高级餐厅于2011年首次获得米其林三星评级，当时它的菜单以精致的荤菜著称。

w.m: adj. 以动物为原料的；荤的

paras.en: However, last year, the restaurant’s co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system.
paras.zh: 然而，去年，餐厅的联合老板兼知名主厨丹尼尔·胡姆以我们的食物体系不可持续为由，大胆决定把肉类撤下菜单。

w.m: n. 共同所有人；联合老板

paras.en: While cow milk is still served for tea and coffee, the menu is almost 100 percent vegan.
paras.zh: 虽然喝茶和咖啡时仍提供牛奶，但菜单几乎百分之百是纯素的。

paras.en: At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that “it wasn’t clear if guests would come”, but called the gamble “a risk worth taking.”
paras.zh: 当时，胡姆承认此举有风险，坦言“不清楚客人会不会来”，但称这次冒险是“值得一冒的风险”。

paras.en: “In view of the climate crisis, I didn’t want to open the same restaurant,” Humm told the Financial Times in an interview.
paras.zh: “鉴于气候危机，我不想再开一家和以前一样的餐厅，”胡姆在接受《金融时报》采访时说。

paras.en: “If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors” for others to follow.
paras.zh: “如果我们能在这样的场合展示吃植物性食物的种种可能，就能打开许多扇门”，让其他人效仿。

w.m: adj. 植物性的；以植物为原料的

paras.en: Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park’s decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin’s 2022 New York guide branding it “a bold vision of luxury dining”.
paras.zh: 如今，这项令人瞩目的新成就证明，麦迪逊公园11号把肉类撤下菜单、拥抱植物性食物的决定是正确的，米其林2022年纽约指南称其为“对奢华餐饮的大胆构想”。

w.m: adj. 令人瞩目的；令人钦佩的

paras.en: “We took the leap to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining restaurant knowing in our hearts this was what we believed in,” stated Humm on Instagram.
paras.zh: “我们勇敢地迈出一步，把麦迪逊公园11号转型为一家植物性高级餐厅，因为我们打心底里知道，这正是我们所信奉的，”胡姆在Instagram上写道。

w.m: 勇敢迈出一步；大胆尝试

paras.en: “Last night, we were honored to be awarded three Michelin stars for the 11th year in a row.
paras.zh: “昨晚，我们荣幸地连续第11年获得米其林三星。

paras.en: I am so grateful to the team members who contributed through its nearly 25-year history.
paras.zh: 我非常感激在餐厅近25年的历史中贡献过力量的团队成员。

paras.en: We are also grateful to our guests and partners who believed in our vision and encouraged us to push harder.”
paras.zh: 我们也感谢相信我们的愿景、鼓励我们更加努力的客人和合作伙伴。”

paras.en: Three Michelin stars is the highest award, given to chefs who are at the peak of their profession.
paras.zh: 米其林三星是最高荣誉，授予处于职业巅峰的厨师。

paras.en: “Their cooking is elevated to an art form and some of their dishes are destined to become classics,” reads Michelin’s website, in a clear nod to plant-based foods’ growing significance in the culinary (烹饪的) world.
paras.zh: “他们的烹饪升华为一种艺术形式，其中一些菜肴注定会成为经典，”米其林网站上写道，这显然是在肯定植物性食物在烹饪界日益重要的地位。

paras.en: “I think luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility,” says Humm.
paras.zh: “我认为奢侈品企业确实可以发挥作用，也负有责任，”胡姆说。

paras.en: “The more creative we are, the more beautiful and delicious our future will be.”
paras.zh: “我们越有创造力，我们的未来就会越美好、越美味。”

passages.name: 2025年12月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 基因检测到底有多准确
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与健康
passages.summary: 基因检测日益流行，但其准确度在很大程度上取决于检测类型、所提的具体问题以及特征背后遗传机制的复杂程度。检测单基因特征、判断两份样本是否属于近亲，结果都比较可靠；而祖源比例几乎反映不出真实的祖源，远亲的判断结果也较模糊。大多数特征和疾病还取决于非遗传因素，多因素特征的检测往往很难解读；声称能匹配恋爱对象或预测性格、天赋的检测则纯属无稽之谈。

paras.en: With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is.
paras.zh: 随着基因检测越来越流行，许多人不禁想知道它到底有多准确。

paras.en: Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn (先天的) health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon.
paras.zh: 无论你做DNA检测是为了构建自己涵盖更广的DNA家谱，还是想获得有关先天健康状况的精确信息，了解基因检测有多准确、哪些信息我们可以信赖，都很重要。

w.m: adj. 扩展的；范围更广的

paras.en: How accurate DNA tests are depends greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait (特征) is.
paras.zh: DNA检测的准确度在很大程度上取决于所做检测的类型、你提出的具体问题，以及某一特征背后的遗传机制有多复杂。

paras.en: For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease-causing trait is present.
paras.zh: 例如，对于取决于单个基因的特征，相关检测能提供可靠得多的结果，因为你能看出某种致病特征是否存在。

paras.en: Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities.
paras.zh: 祖源检测声称能揭示我们的基因身份。

paras.en: But saying you are 30 percent East Asian or American hardly reflects your real ancestry.
paras.zh: 但说你30%是东亚人或美洲人，几乎反映不出你真正的祖源。

paras.en: What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members?
paras.zh: 那么，用DNA检测来寻找远房亲属又如何呢？

w.m: adj. 远房的；（亲属关系）远的

paras.en: There are tools to compare one’s DNA with others’ to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification.
paras.zh: 有些工具能把一个人的DNA与他人的DNA相比对，根据基因鉴定结果找到远亲。

w.m: adj. 远房的；（亲属关系）远的

paras.en: These kinds of applications are generally accurate.
paras.zh: 这类应用通常是准确的。

paras.en: It’s relatively easy to tell whether two DNA samples belong to close relatives.
paras.zh: 要判断两份DNA样本是否属于近亲，相对容易。

paras.en: With distant relatives, results become hazier.
paras.zh: 至于远亲，结果就变得更模糊了。

w.m: adj. 远房的；（亲属关系）远的

paras.en: Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary (遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions.
paras.zh: 基因健康检测声称能够检测出某些遗传疾病或其他健康状况。

paras.en: While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone.
paras.zh: 虽然某些罕见疾病很容易识别出来，但大多数潜在的健康状况仅靠基因检测是无法识别的。

paras.en: The large majority of our traits and diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others.
paras.zh: 我们绝大多数的特征和疾病还取决于非遗传因素，比如生活方式、环境以及其他许多因素。

paras.en: Genetic tests for multi-factorial traits are often very tricky to interpret.
paras.zh: 针对多因素特征的基因检测往往很难解读。

paras.en: Height, for example, depends on hundreds of genes, each contributing a little to the outcome, together with a bunch of environmental factors.
paras.zh: 例如，身高取决于数百个基因，每个基因都对最终结果起一点作用，此外还取决于一系列环境因素。

paras.en: A test can look at many genes at once, but it’s difficult to predict how they will play together.
paras.zh: 一项检测可以同时考察许多基因，但很难预测它们会如何共同起作用。

paras.en: Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA.
paras.zh: 此外，你还应该考虑到那些没有写在DNA里的非遗传因素。

paras.en: Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense.
paras.zh: 那些号称能帮你找到完美恋爱对象的检测，以及那些声称能根据你的DNA预测性格或天赋的检测，纯属无稽之谈。

w.m: v. 提出（做某事）；表示愿意
n. 般配的人；（恋爱）对象

paras.en: At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak.
paras.zh: 目前，这些应用的科学依据要么根本不存在，要么极其薄弱。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 有机食品值得多花钱吗
passages.genre: 议论文 · 食品与农业
passages.summary: 是否购买有机食品是个人的选择，科学对有机食品是否“更好”给不出明确答案。有机食品与常规种植的食品营养价值相同，农药残留不一定更少，食品安全上也没有大的差别；有机农业对环境的影响可能更小，但土地利用效率低得多。有机农业的支持者认为，若投入同样多的研究和资金，其产量和效率可能大幅提高。

paras.en: Is organic food worth the higher price?
paras.zh: 有机食品值得花更高的价钱吗？

paras.en: It’s the classic grocery store dilemma.
paras.zh: 这是在杂货店购物时常见的两难选择。

w.m: n. 两难境地；进退两难

paras.en: On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best.
paras.zh: 一方面，你家的餐桌只配摆上最好的东西。

paras.en: On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far.
paras.zh: 另一方面，你的钱包也只能撑到这个份上。

w.m: 只能维持到一定程度；（钱）只够用这么多

paras.en: Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food, Agricultural and Resource Economics.
paras.zh: 食品、农业与资源经济学教授迈克·冯·马索说，买不买有机食品是个人的决定。

w.m: prep. 冯（德语等人名中的姓氏前缀）

paras.en: Science won’t give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is “better.”
paras.zh: 对于有机食品是否“更好”这个问题，科学不会给出明确的答案。

paras.en: There are often trade-offs (权衡), and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration.
paras.zh: 这其中常常需要权衡取舍，而且根据所考虑的产品不同，答案也会变得不那么确定。

paras.en: One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious.
paras.zh: 有一点是确定的：有机食品和常规种植的食品营养价值相同。

paras.en: From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products.
paras.zh: 从营养角度看，有机产品和传统种植的产品没有区别。

paras.en: Organic products don’t necessarily have fewer pesticides (杀虫剂)—in fact, they may have more.
paras.zh: 有机产品的农药不一定更少——事实上，可能还更多。

paras.en: There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective.
paras.zh: 从食品安全角度看，有机产品和非有机产品之间也没有大的差别。

paras.en: Even organic growers use pesticides.
paras.zh: 就连有机种植者也使用农药。

paras.en: Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products.
paras.zh: 检测表明，常规种植的产品上即便有农药残留，也微乎其微。

paras.en: In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers.
paras.zh: 事实上，有机农场主使用的农药往往量更大，因为他们只能使用天然的杀虫剂。

paras.en: Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests (害虫) than any single natural pesticide.
paras.zh: 化学农药能杀灭的害虫种类通常比任何一种天然农药都要广得多。

w.m: 范围广泛的；各种各样的

paras.en: The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella.
paras.zh: 有机农业中使用动物粪便，也可能成为大肠杆菌、沙门氏菌等细菌传播的一个因素。

paras.en: Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products.
paras.zh: 过去10年间，按比例计算，加拿大有机产品因食品安全问题被召回的次数比常规产品更多。

w.m: adv. 按比例地；相对而言

paras.en: On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint.
paras.zh: 总体而言，有机农业对环境的影响可能更小。

paras.en: That’s mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower.
paras.zh: 这主要是因为有机耕作造成地下水污染的风险更低。

paras.en: Organic farmers have never used neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide.
paras.zh: 有机农场主从未使用过新烟碱类农药，这类农药颇具争议，被认为与全球蜜蜂数量减少有关。

paras.en: Traditional agriculture has been making “dramatic improvements” to reduce its impact on the environment.
paras.zh: 传统农业一直在取得“显著的改进”，以减少其对环境的影响。

paras.en: It isn’t a black-and-white picture, though.
paras.zh: 不过，情况并非非黑即白。

w.m: adj. 非黑即白的；黑白分明的

paras.en: Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop.
paras.zh: 在土地利用方面，有机耕作的效率要低得多，不过产量因作物不同而差异相当大。

paras.en: On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does to conventional agriculture.
paras.zh: 另一方面，有机农业的倡导者认为，如果食品行业像对常规农业那样，向有机农业投入同样多的研究和资金，其产量和效率可能会大幅提高。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 人类合作与自私的根源
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与遗传
passages.summary: 人类本质上是慷慨还是自私、这些倾向由基因还是环境塑造，至今仍有争议。文章介绍了相关研究：人性中既有合作的一面，也有自私的一面；双胞胎研究和基因研究表明基因会影响行为，进化科学家也对合作行为的起源提出了几种可能的解释。不过，几乎没有哪种行为完全由基因决定，合作或自私的程度因人而异，取决于遗传和环境的多种影响。

paras.en: It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment.
paras.zh: 我们在本质上是慷慨还是自私，这些倾向是由基因还是由环境塑造的，至今仍有争议。

paras.en: Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative.
paras.zh: 一些证据表明，人类生来就乐于合作。

w.m: adj. 合作的；乐于合作的

paras.en: At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need.
paras.zh: 到了人生的后续阶段，我们常常通力合作以实现目标，并在有需要时伸出援手。

w.m: 在需要的时候；在危难时

paras.en: Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plentiful.
paras.zh: 然而，自私行为的事例也比比皆是。

paras.en: One recent study tested people’s willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good.
paras.zh: 最近一项研究测试了人们为实现更大的利益而搁置一己私利的意愿。

paras.en: It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating.
paras.zh: 研究发现，自私比合作更有利。

paras.en: The benefit may be short-lived, however.
paras.zh: 不过，这种好处可能只是暂时的。

paras.en: Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run.
paras.zh: 另一项研究表明，从长远来看，选择合作的参与者表现更好。

w.m: n. （游戏、比赛的）参与者；玩家

paras.en: It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits (特征).
paras.zh: 人性似乎既容得下亲社会特征，也容得下自私特征。

paras.en: Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots.
paras.zh: 遗传学研究在确定这些特征的生物学根源方面已经取得了一些进展。

paras.en: By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors.
paras.zh: 同卵双胞胎共有近100%的基因，异卵双胞胎则共有约一半；研究人员通过比较这两类双胞胎，发现了压倒性的证据，证明基因会对行为产生影响。

w.m: adj. 同卵的；完全相同的
n. 双胞胎之一；（复数）双胞胎
adj. 异卵的；不完全相同的

paras.en: In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer.
paras.zh: 例如，在这些双胞胎研究中，同卵双胞胎和异卵双胞胎需要与一名同伴分一笔钱。

w.m: n. 双胞胎之一；（复数）双胞胎
adj. 同卵的；完全相同的
adj. 异卵的；不完全相同的

paras.en: Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis.
paras.zh: 这类研究往往还依靠细致的心理评估和DNA分析。

paras.en: Other work highlights specific genes as key players.
paras.zh: 另一些研究则着重指出，某些特定基因起着关键作用。

w.m: 起关键作用者；关键角色

paras.en: My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic (利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers.
paras.zh: 我和同事们最近鉴定出一个与利他行为相关的基因，并发现它的一种特定变体与学龄前儿童更自私的行为有关。

paras.en: According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line.
paras.zh: 据进化科学家称，合作行为可能最先在亲属之间演化出来，以促进其基因世系的延续。

paras.en: As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood.
paras.zh: 随着社群日益多样化，相互扶持的范围可能已经扩大，把没有血缘关系的个体也纳入其中。

paras.en: Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation.
paras.zh: 另一种可能是，人类合作是为了获得某种好处，比如提升声誉。

paras.en: Finally, evolutionary processes may also take place at the group level.
paras.zh: 最后，进化过程也可能发生在群体层面。

paras.en: Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups.
paras.zh: 由高度合作的个体组成的群体生存几率更高，因为他们能够齐心协力，实现合作程度较低的群体无法达到的目标。

w.m: adj. 无法达到的；难以实现的

paras.en: Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins.
paras.zh: 然而，几乎没有哪种行为完全由基因决定，即使在同卵双胞胎中也是如此。

w.m: adj. 由基因决定的；遗传的
adj. 同卵的；完全相同的
n. 双胞胎之一；（复数）双胞胎

paras.en: Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation.
paras.zh: 文化、学校教育和养育方式是合作的重要决定因素。

paras.en: Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.
paras.zh: 因此，我们行事时合作或自私的程度因人而异，取决于多种遗传因素和环境因素的影响。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 低估自我的“冒名顶替现象”
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与健康
passages.summary: 患有“冒名顶替现象”的人一贯低估自己，把成功归因于外部环境或运气，并担心自己的“骗局”被揭穿。哈勒-维滕贝格马丁·路德大学的心理学家首次在真实生活条件下研究了这一现象，发现自我报告的冒名顶替现象程度与实际智力或表现无关，也与年龄和性别无关；研究还支持了这样的假设：有这种倾向的人会贬低自己的表现，把正面结果归因于外部原因。这种现象不被界定为精神疾病，但受其困扰的人更容易患抑郁症。

paras.en: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon.
paras.zh: 那些一贯低估自己、低估自身表现的人，受所谓“冒名顶替现象”的困扰。

paras.en: They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance.
paras.zh: 他们认为，任何成功都归因于外部环境，或者仅仅是运气和偶然。

paras.en: Those people live in constant fear that their “deception” will be exposed.
paras.zh: 这些人时刻生活在恐惧中，担心自己的“骗局”会被揭穿。

paras.en: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again.
paras.zh: 人们时不时怀疑自己的能力，这很常见。

paras.en: A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively.
paras.zh: 适度的反思和自我怀疑能够防止人冲动行事。

paras.en: However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance.
paras.zh: 然而，有些人尽管表现良好，却一直饱受大量自我怀疑的困扰。

paras.en: They think that none of their successes are a product of their skill or hard work; instead, they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others.
paras.zh: 他们认为，自己的成功没有一项是自身技能或努力的结果；而是把成功归因于外部环境，比如运气和偶然，或者认为别人大大高估了自己的表现。

paras.en: Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.
paras.zh: 另一方面，他们总是把失败内化为自身缺点的结果。

paras.en: Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions.
paras.zh: 哈勒-维滕贝格马丁·路德大学的心理学家首次在真实生活条件下研究了这一课题。

paras.en: Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance.
paras.zh: 76名参与者完成了一系列智力测试，并且无论实际表现如何，都收到了关于测试的正面反馈。

paras.en: They were then asked why they thought they did so well.
paras.zh: 随后，他们被问及为什么认为自己表现得这么好。

paras.en: The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance.
paras.zh: 研究显示了两点：第一，自我报告的冒名顶替现象程度与实际测得的智力或表现无关。

paras.en: Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities.
paras.zh: 第二，该测试支持了这样一个假设：倾向于表现出冒名顶替现象的人会贬低自己经客观测量的表现，并把正面结果归因于运气和偶然等外部原因，而不是归因于自己的能力。

paras.en: These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.
paras.zh: 这些结果也与年龄和性别完全无关。

paras.en: A permanent underestimation of one’s own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this.
paras.zh: 长期低估自身能力，往往伴随着这样的恐惧：担心这种想象中的智力骗局迟早会被揭穿，而自己会为此付出代价。

paras.en: The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by U.S. psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes.
paras.zh: 1978年，美国心理学家葆琳·克兰斯和苏珊娜·艾姆斯首次描述了冒名顶替现象。

paras.en: They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent.
paras.zh: 她们观察到，不认为自己很聪明的成功女性特别多。

paras.en: The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness.
paras.zh: 冒名顶替现象并未被界定为一种精神疾病。

paras.en: However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.
paras.zh: 然而，受其困扰的人更容易患抑郁症。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 音乐：跨越文化的共同语言
passages.genre: 议论文 · 艺术与文化
passages.summary: 作者认为音乐是一种世界通用的语言，每种文化、每个国家都有音乐。五声音阶为许多文化所共有，让各地音乐人得以交流、相互理解。尽管各文化的音乐风格不同，音乐的用途却大同小异，这种对音乐的共同热爱能把人们团结在一起。

paras.en: Music is a universal language.
paras.zh: 音乐是一种世界通用的语言。

paras.en: In every culture and country, you will find music.
paras.zh: 在每一种文化、每一个国家，你都能找到音乐。

paras.en: It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony.
paras.zh: 音乐在全世界都极其重要，并且有可能让人们和平、和谐地相聚在一起。

paras.en: One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group.
paras.zh: 在音乐方面，我最喜欢的经历之一，就是看到来自不同文化的音乐人走到一起，作为一个整体同台演出。

paras.en: When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved.
paras.zh: 当每种文化都为这个整体带来自己独特的品质时，就会形成一种全新的声音。

paras.en: This can create extraordinary results.
paras.zh: 这能创造出非凡的成果。

w.m: adj. 非凡的；非同寻常的

paras.en: People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.
paras.zh: 人们可以把音乐当作共同语言，彼此交流。

paras.en: One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale.
paras.zh: 不同文化之间有一条共同的音乐纽带，被称为五声音阶。

paras.en: It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music.
paras.zh: 竟有这么多文化在处理音乐时共同使用这一工具，真令人惊讶。

paras.en: The pentatonic scale consists of five notes: “penta-” meaning five, and “tonic” meaning tone or note.
paras.zh: 五声音阶由五个音组成：“penta-”的意思是“五”，“tonic”的意思是“音调”或“音”。

paras.en: This scale can be found in music everywhere, including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians.
paras.zh: 这种音阶在世界各地的音乐中都能找到，包括美洲原住民、非洲人和亚洲人的音乐。

paras.en: It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock.
paras.zh: 流行音乐、布鲁斯、爵士乐和摇滚乐中也能找到它。

paras.en: Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.
paras.zh: 借助这种五声音阶，来自全球各地的音乐人有了一种媒介，可以通过它相互关联、交流、合奏，并最终相互理解。

w.m: v. 相互关联；产生共鸣

paras.en: Music is tied to specific perceptual (感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics (美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos).
paras.zh: 音乐与特定的感知、心智和情感能力紧密相连，包括语言（所有社会都为自己的歌曲配上歌词）、运动控制（所有社会的人都会跳舞）、声音分析（所有音乐体系都有鲜明的音高和音质）以及美感（其曲调和节奏在重复与混乱之间保持平衡）。

w.m: adj. 运动的；运动神经的

paras.en: There is no known society that existed without music.
paras.zh: 在已知的社会中，没有哪一个是在没有音乐的情况下存在过的。

paras.en: Although each culture has its own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board.
paras.zh: 尽管每种文化在音乐上都有自己特定的风格和方式，但你会发现，音乐背后的用途总体上非常相似。

paras.en: Music essentially serves to express or change emotions.
paras.zh: 音乐的本质作用是表达或改变情绪。

paras.en: It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you.
paras.zh: 它能让你振奋，让你悲伤，让你愤怒，也能让你兴奋。

paras.en: Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration.
paras.zh: 音乐常常带有仪式性：用于宗教、仪式和庆典。

paras.en: Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun.
paras.zh: 音乐也可以纯粹是消遣性的：娱乐身心、令人愉快、充满乐趣。

w.m: adj. 有娱乐性的；使人愉快的

paras.en: Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way.
paras.zh: 无论你以何种方式用过音乐，几乎可以肯定，其他每一种文化都以完全相同的方式用过音乐。

paras.en: And that is something that bonds all of us.
paras.zh: 而正是这一点把我们所有人联系在一起。

w.m: v. 使结合；使紧密联系

paras.en: We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.
paras.zh: 我们都对音乐怀有深深的热爱，而音乐有力量把我们团结起来。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 孩子如何理解道德厌恶
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与成长
passages.summary: 厌恶是人类普遍的情绪，分为生理厌恶和道德厌恶，但并非所有学者都认为道德厌恶真的存在。研究者让母亲与孩子讨论有关两类厌恶的故事，初步发现她们主要谈论生理厌恶，并把道德上的错误行为与愤怒而不是厌恶联系起来。研究者认为，对八岁及以下的儿童来说，道德厌恶要么更晚才能理解，要么即便使用也只是一种比喻。

paras.en: Disgust is a universal human emotion.
paras.zh: 厌恶是人类普遍具有的一种情绪。

paras.en: One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects.
paras.zh: 有一种厌恶叫作生理厌恶，它保护我们，使我们不去吃或触碰可能对我们有危险的东西，比如生肉或昆虫。

paras.en: Children experience physical disgust from a very early age, but do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old.
paras.zh: 孩子很小的时候就会体验到生理厌恶，但要到四岁左右才能理解这个概念。

paras.en: Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong.
paras.zh: 一些研究者坚持认为还存在另一种厌恶，叫作道德厌恶，它保护我们，使我们不去从事那些可能被视为道德上错误的活动。

paras.en: Examples of things that cause moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.
paras.zh: 引起道德厌恶的事情有偷窃、撒谎或作弊等。

paras.en: However, not all academics think that moral disgust really exists.
paras.zh: 然而，并非所有学者都认为道德厌恶真的存在。

paras.en: Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor (隐喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.
paras.zh: 有些人说，当我们在道德问题上提到厌恶时，我们是把厌恶当作一种比喻来用，而我们实际感受到的是愤怒。

paras.en: If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it.
paras.zh: 如果道德厌恶在成长过程中出现得相当晚，那么认为它其实带有社会性成分，就是合乎情理的。

paras.en: Children learn about emotions in many different ways.
paras.zh: 孩子通过许多不同的途径了解情绪。

paras.en: Of special relevance are parent-child conversations about emotions.
paras.zh: 尤为相关的是父母与孩子之间关于情绪的对话。

w.m: adj. 父母与孩子之间的；亲子的

paras.en: Indeed, children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.
paras.zh: 事实上，父母经常谈论情绪的孩子，比父母不常讨论情绪的孩子对情绪理解得更好。

paras.en: However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust.
paras.zh: 然而，还没有研究考察过父母和孩子是如何谈论厌恶的。

paras.en: This is what we set out to examine in our study.
paras.zh: 这正是我们在研究中着手考察的问题。

paras.en: We asked 68 English-speaking mothers and their four-, six-, or eight-year-old children to discuss some stories about moral and physical disgust.
paras.zh: 我们请68位说英语的母亲和她们四岁、六岁或八岁的孩子讨论一些关于道德厌恶和生理厌恶的故事。

paras.en: Our preliminary findings show mothers and children do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.
paras.zh: 我们的初步研究结果显示，母亲和孩子确实会谈论厌恶，但主要谈的是生理厌恶，而不太谈道德厌恶。

paras.en: When we asked mothers and children to discuss moral issues, such as whether it is OK to play with a child who has stolen someone else’s snack, they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.
paras.zh: 当我们让母亲和孩子讨论道德问题时，比如可不可以和一个偷了别人零食的孩子一起玩，他们把这类道德上的错误行为与愤怒这种情绪而不是厌恶联系在一起。

paras.en: Does this mean that moral disgust does not exist?
paras.zh: 这是否意味着道德厌恶并不存在？

paras.en: Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults.
paras.zh: 一些研究者认为，成年人身上存在道德厌恶。

paras.en: Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years.
paras.zh: 我们的研究结果表明，在年龄大至八岁的孩子身上，道德厌恶要么要到更大的年龄才能理解，要么即便用到，也只是一种比喻用法。

w.m: 即便有的话；即便如此（也）

passages.name: 2026年6月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 误以为对方了解自己会让人更诚实
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与社会
passages.summary: 《自然》杂志最近的一项研究发现，人们了解到陌生人的情况后，会误以为对方也了解自己，因此表现得更诚实。研究人员在贫困地区的住宅小区分发介绍当地社区警察的传单，结果收到传单的居民认为警察发现违法活动的可能性更大；而且传单刚一发放，这些小区周边的刑事投诉和逮捕都少于对照小区周边。

paras.en: After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us.
paras.zh: 了解到一个陌生人的详细情况后，我们会误以为对方也了解我们。

paras.en: As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.
paras.zh: 《自然》杂志最近的一项研究表明，正因如此，我们在对方身边会表现得更诚实。

paras.en: Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal (相互的).
paras.zh: 以往的研究发现，我们往往会认为社会关系是相互的。

paras.en: Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too.
paras.zh: 大多数时候，这种看法是准确的：你视为朋友的人，通常也会把你当作朋友。

paras.en: But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn’t know you at all.
paras.zh: 但有时，我们的社会联系更偏向单方面：比如，你可能了解到某个陌生人的一些情况，而对方根本不认识你。

paras.en: Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.
paras.zh: 研究人员阿努杰·沙阿和迈克尔·拉福雷斯特想知道，我们认为社会联系是相互的这种倾向，是否会让我们误以为某个陌生人真的了解我们。

paras.en: In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found.
paras.zh: 在一系列实验室研究中，研究人员发现的正是这种情况。

paras.en: When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us.
paras.zh: 我们了解陌生人时，会错误地以为他们也了解我们。

paras.en: But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment.
paras.zh: 但真正有意思的发现，出现在研究人员走出实验室、开展实地实验的时候。

paras.en: The team developed leaflets (传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force.
paras.zh: 研究团队制作了传单，上面印着当地社区警察相当普通的一些信息，比如他们最喜欢的食物、爱好或加入警队的原因。

paras.en: They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas.
paras.zh: 随后，他们把这些传单送到贫困地区若干住宅小区的每一户。

paras.en: The officers themselves also dropped off cards containing similar information for local residents.
paras.zh: 警察本人也给当地居民送去了载有类似信息的卡片。

paras.en: Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards.
paras.zh: 两个月后，研究人员调查了这些住宅小区的居民，也调查了对照地区的居民，对照地区既没收到传单，也没收到外联卡片。

w.m: n. 外联；（社区）外展服务

paras.en: Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and to say how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it.
paras.zh: 研究人员请居民想象自己犯了罪，并说出当地警察查出此事的可能性有多大。

paras.en: They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.
paras.zh: 居民们还评估了该地区的警察对自己有多了解。

paras.en: The team found that residents of the developments that had received the leaflets believed it more likely that local officers would find out about illegal activity than residents of the control areas.
paras.zh: 研究团队发现，与对照地区的居民相比，收到过传单的住宅小区的居民认为当地警察发现违法活动的可能性更大。

paras.en: Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.
paras.zh: 更引人注目的是，研究团队发现，传单刚一发放，收到传单的住宅小区周边地区的刑事投诉和逮捕就都比对照小区周边少。

w.m: adv. 引人注目地；显著地
